questions.text: In 'A Letter to God', why does Lencho call the post office employees 'a bunch of crooks'?
options: They refused to deliver his letter to God
He believed they had kept part of the money God sent him
They laughed at him when he posted the letter
They charged him extra postage for his second letter
questions.explanation: The postmaster could collect only 70 of the 100 pesos Lencho asked for. Lencho's faith in God was so complete that he assumed the employees had stolen the rest — the story's central irony, since they were the ones who helped him.

questions.chapter: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom
questions.text: According to Nelson Mandela, what are the 'twin obligations' that every man has?
options: To his religion and to his government
To his teachers and to his elders
To his career and to his personal freedom
To his family and to his people and country
questions.explanation: Mandela says every man has obligations to his family (parents, wife and children) and to his people, community and country. Under apartheid, it was almost impossible for a man of colour to fulfil both.

questions.text: In 'His First Flight', what finally made the young seagull fly?
options: Hunger — he dived at a piece of fish his mother held just out of reach
His brothers pushed him off the ledge
A strong gust of wind swept him off the cliff
His father carried him down to the sea
questions.explanation: His mother hovered near the ledge with a piece of fish and stopped just short of him. Maddened by hunger, he dived at the food, and as he fell his wings spread out and he flew.

questions.chapter: From the Diary of Anne Frank
questions.text: What name did Anne Frank give to her diary?
questions.explanation: Anne felt she had no true friend to confide in, so she wanted the diary itself to be that friend. She named it Kitty and wrote her entries as letters to her.

questions.text: In 'The Sermon at Benares', what did the Buddha ask Kisa Gotami to bring?
options: Water from the holy river Ganga
A flower from the Bodhi tree
A handful of mustard seed from a house where no one had lost a loved one
questions.explanation: Going from house to house, Kisa Gotami found that every family had lost someone. She realised that death is common to all, and that grieving over it only brings more pain.

questions.text: In Robert Frost's 'Dust of Snow', what shakes the dust of snow down on the poet?
options: A crow sitting on a hemlock tree
A sparrow on a pine tree
A child playing in the snow
The wind blowing through an oak tree
questions.explanation: A crow on a hemlock tree shakes snow onto the poet. Frost uses these usually gloomy symbols to show that even a small, ordinary moment can change one's mood and save a day that was going badly.

questions.text: In 'Fire and Ice', what do 'fire' and 'ice' stand for?
questions.explanation: Fire represents desire — greed, lust and ambition — while ice represents hatred, which is cold and rigid. Frost suggests that either emotion is powerful enough to destroy the world.

questions.text: In 'The Ball Poem', what does the poet mean when he says the boy is learning 'the epistemology of loss'?
options: How to buy a new ball with his own money
That balls are easily lost near the harbour
How to hide his feelings from adults
What loss really means and how to live with it
questions.explanation: Epistemology is the study of knowledge. By losing his ball, the boy learns for the first time that some things are lost forever and that he must learn to bear the loss himself — something money cannot buy back.

questions.text: In 'A Tiger in the Zoo', where does the poet say the tiger should ideally be?
options: Lurking in the shadow of long grass near a water hole
Sleeping safely inside a concrete cell
Performing tricks in a circus ring
Resting on a snowy mountain top
questions.explanation: Leslie Norris contrasts the caged tiger with its natural life: it should be sliding through long grass near the water hole where plump deer pass, not pacing helplessly behind bars.

questions.text: Why did Hari Singh return to Anil's room after stealing his money?
options: The police had already caught him at the station
He wanted to steal more money the next day
He realised Anil's trust and the chance to be educated were worth more than the money
Anil had promised him a reward for coming back
questions.explanation: Anil was teaching Hari to read, write and add numbers. Hari realised that being educated could make him a 'big man' one day, and that losing Anil's trust was a far greater loss than the stolen money.

questions.text: How did Ausable, the secret agent, get rid of Max in 'The Midnight Visitor'?
options: He overpowered Max and tied him up
He tricked Max into climbing out onto a balcony that did not exist
He called the police on the hotel telephone
He handed Max a fake report and let him leave
questions.explanation: Ausable invented a balcony below the window and claimed the police were knocking. Max jumped out onto the 'balcony' and fell, while the knock was only a waiter bringing the drinks Ausable had ordered.

questions.text: What was Bholi's real name?
questions.explanation: Bholi was born Sulekha, but a fall from a cot as a baby and an attack of smallpox left her slow and pockmarked, so everyone called her Bholi, 'the simpleton'. Education later gave her the confidence to speak up.

questions.text: Choose the correct option: By the time we reached the station, the train ____.
questions.explanation: When two actions happened in the past, the earlier one takes the past perfect (had + past participle). The train left before we reached, so 'had already left' is correct.

questions.text: Fill in the blank with a suitable modal: You ____ wear a helmet while riding a motorcycle; it is the law.
questions.explanation: 'Must' expresses an obligation or a rule that has to be followed. 'Might' and 'could' show possibility, and 'would' is used for conditions or polite requests.

questions.text: Choose the correct verb: Neither the teacher nor the students ____ aware of the change in the timetable.
questions.explanation: With 'neither … nor' and 'either … or', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. Here that is 'students', which is plural, so 'were' is correct.

questions.text: Choose the correct reported speech: He asked me, “Have you completed the project?”
options: He asked me that had I completed the project.
He asked me if I have completed the project.
He asked me had I completed the project?
He asked me if I had completed the project.
questions.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with 'if' or 'whether', in statement word order and without a question mark. The present perfect 'have completed' shifts back to the past perfect 'had completed'.

questions.text: The HCF of two numbers is 6 and their LCM is 180. If one of the numbers is 30, what is the other number?
questions.explanation: For any two positive integers, HCF × LCM = product of the numbers. So the other number = (6 × 180) ÷ 30 = 1080 ÷ 30 = 36.

questions.text: If α and β are the zeroes of the polynomial x² − 5x + 6, what is the value of α² + β²?
questions.explanation: For ax² + bx + c, α + β = −b/a = 5 and αβ = c/a = 6. So α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ = 25 − 12 = 13. (Check: the zeroes are 2 and 3, and 4 + 9 = 13.)

questions.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
questions.text: For what value of k will the pair of equations 2x + 3y = 7 and 4x + ky = 14 have infinitely many solutions?
questions.explanation: Infinitely many solutions need a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂. Here 2/4 = 7/14 = 1/2, so 3/k = 1/2, which gives k = 6.

questions.text: What is the nature of the roots of the quadratic equation 2x² − 4x + 3 = 0?
questions.explanation: The discriminant D = b² − 4ac = (−4)² − 4(2)(3) = 16 − 24 = −8. Since D < 0, the equation has no real roots.

questions.text: For what value of k does the equation kx² − 6x + 1 = 0 have two equal roots?
questions.explanation: Equal roots occur when the discriminant is zero: b² − 4ac = 36 − 4k = 0, so k = 9.

questions.text: What is the 10th term of the AP 2, 7, 12, 17, …?
questions.explanation: Here a = 2 and d = 5. Using aₙ = a + (n − 1)d, a₁₀ = 2 + 9 × 5 = 47.

questions.text: How many terms of the AP 9, 17, 25, … must be taken to give a sum of 636?
questions.explanation: With a = 9 and d = 8, Sₙ = n/2 [2(9) + (n − 1)8] = n(4n + 5). Setting n(4n + 5) = 636 gives 4n² + 5n − 636 = 0, whose positive root is n = 12.

questions.text: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC with D on AB and E on AC. If AD = 3 cm, DB = 6 cm and AE = 4 cm, what is EC?
questions.explanation: By the Basic Proportionality Theorem, AD/DB = AE/EC. So 3/6 = 4/EC, which gives EC = 8 cm.

questions.text: What is the distance between the points (2, 3) and (5, 7)?
Find the coordinates of the point that divides the line segment joining (−1, 7) and (4, −3) in the ratio 2 : 3.
questions.explanation: By the section formula, x = (2 × 4 + 3 × (−1)) ÷ 5 = 1 and y = (2 × (−3) + 3 × 7) ÷ 5 = 3. So the point is (1, 3).

questions.text: From a point Q, the length of the tangent to a circle is 4 cm and the distance of Q from the centre is 5 cm. What is the radius of the circle?
questions.explanation: The radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact, so radius² + tangent² = distance². Radius = √(5² − 4²) = √9 = 3 cm.

questions.text: If sin A = 3/5 and A is an acute angle, what is the value of cos A?
questions.explanation: Using sin²A + cos²A = 1, cos²A = 1 − 9/25 = 16/25, so cos A = 4/5 (positive because A is acute).

questions.text: What is the value of (1 + tan²θ)(1 − sin θ)(1 + sin θ)?
questions.explanation: 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ and (1 − sin θ)(1 + sin θ) = 1 − sin²θ = cos²θ. So the expression is sec²θ × cos²θ = 1.

questions.text: From a point on the ground 30 m away from the foot of a vertical tower, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is 60°. What is the height of the tower?
questions.explanation: tan 60° = height ÷ 30 and tan 60° = √3, so height = 30√3 m (about 51.96 m).

questions.text: What is the area of a sector of a circle of radius 6 cm whose central angle is 60°? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: Area of sector = (θ/360°) × πr² = (60/360) × (22/7) × 36 = 132/7 cm², which is about 18.86 cm².

questions.text: Two cubes, each of volume 64 cm³, are joined end to end. What is the surface area of the resulting cuboid?
questions.explanation: Each cube has edge ∛64 = 4 cm, so the cuboid measures 8 cm × 4 cm × 4 cm. Its surface area = 2(lb + bh + hl) = 2(32 + 16 + 32) = 160 cm².

questions.text: For a grouped frequency distribution, the modal class is 30–40. The frequency of the modal class is 12, of the class before it 8, and of the class after it 6. What is the mode?
Two dice are thrown at the same time. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers on top is 8?
questions.explanation: There are 36 equally likely outcomes. A sum of 8 comes from (2, 6), (3, 5), (4, 4), (5, 3) and (6, 2) — 5 outcomes — so P = 5/36.

questions.text: What is the power of a convex lens of focal length 20 cm?
questions.explanation: Power P = 1/f, with f in metres. For a convex lens f = +0.20 m, so P = 1/0.20 = +5 dioptres.

questions.text: An object is placed 15 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm. Where is the image formed?
options: 30 cm in front of the mirror
6 cm in front of the mirror
questions.explanation: Using 1/v + 1/u = 1/f with u = −15 cm and f = −10 cm: 1/v = −1/10 + 1/15 = −1/30, so v = −30 cm. The negative sign means a real image 30 cm in front of the mirror.

questions.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.text: Which defect of vision is corrected by using a concave lens of suitable power?
questions.explanation: In myopia (near-sightedness), the image of distant objects forms in front of the retina. A concave (diverging) lens spreads the rays slightly so that the image forms on the retina.

questions.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.text: Why does the clear sky appear blue?
options: Blue light travels faster through air than other colours
Air absorbs all colours except blue
The sky reflects the colour of the oceans
Fine particles in the atmosphere scatter blue light more than red light
questions.explanation: Air molecules and fine particles are smaller than the wavelength of visible light, so they scatter shorter wavelengths (blue) much more strongly than longer ones (red). This scattered blue light reaches our eyes from all directions.

questions.text: Three resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω and 6 Ω are connected in parallel. What is their equivalent resistance?
questions.explanation: For resistors in parallel, 1/R = 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6 = 3/6 + 2/6 + 1/6 = 1, so R = 1 Ω — less than the smallest individual resistance, as expected.

questions.text: An electric iron of 500 W is used for 2 hours every day. How many units of electrical energy does it consume in 30 days?
questions.explanation: Energy = power × time = 0.5 kW × 2 h × 30 = 30 kWh. One 'unit' of electricity is 1 kWh, so the iron uses 30 units.

questions.text: Which rule gives the direction of the force on a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field?
questions.explanation: In Fleming's left-hand rule, the forefinger points along the magnetic field and the middle finger along the current; the thumb then gives the direction of the force (motion) on the conductor.

questions.text: What type of reaction is Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu?
questions.explanation: Iron is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from copper sulphate solution. The blue solution turns pale green (FeSO₄) and a brown coating of copper forms on the iron.

questions.text: In the reaction CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O, which substance is oxidised?
questions.explanation: Oxidation is the gain of oxygen (or loss of hydrogen). Hydrogen gains oxygen to form water, so H₂ is oxidised, while copper oxide loses oxygen and is reduced.

questions.text: A solution turns red litmus blue. Which of these could be its pH?
questions.explanation: Turning red litmus blue shows that the solution is basic, and basic solutions have a pH greater than 7. A pH of 7 is neutral and values below 7 are acidic.

questions.text: What is the chemical formula of Plaster of Paris?
questions.explanation: Plaster of Paris is calcium sulphate hemihydrate, CaSO₄·½H₂O. It is made by heating gypsum (CaSO₄·2H₂O) at 373 K, and it sets back into gypsum when mixed with water.

questions.text: Which of these metals does NOT produce hydrogen gas when added to dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.explanation: Copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it cannot displace hydrogen from dilute acids. Zinc, magnesium and iron are more reactive than hydrogen and release H₂ gas.

questions.text: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CHO?
questions.explanation: The molecule has three carbon atoms (prop-) and an aldehyde group (–CHO), which takes the suffix '-al'. So it is propanal; propanone is a ketone and propanol is an alcohol.

questions.text: How many covalent bonds are present in a molecule of ethane (C₂H₆)?
questions.explanation: Ethane has one C–C single bond and six C–H single bonds, giving 1 + 6 = 7 covalent bonds.

questions.text: Where does the breakdown of glucose into pyruvate take place during respiration?
questions.explanation: The first step of respiration — splitting six-carbon glucose into three-carbon pyruvate — happens in the cytoplasm. In the presence of oxygen, pyruvate is broken down further in the mitochondria.

questions.text: What is the basic filtration unit of the human kidney called?
questions.explanation: Each kidney contains a large number of nephrons. In each nephron, blood is filtered in the glomerulus, and useful substances are reabsorbed as the filtrate moves along the tubule.

questions.text: Which plant hormone promotes cell division?
questions.explanation: Cytokinins promote cell division and are present in high concentration where cells divide rapidly, such as in fruits and seeds. Auxins promote cell elongation, gibberellins help stem growth, and abscisic acid inhibits growth.

questions.text: Which part of the brain maintains the posture and balance of the body?
questions.explanation: The cerebellum, part of the hindbrain, controls the precision of voluntary actions and maintains posture and balance. The medulla controls involuntary actions such as blood pressure and vomiting.

questions.text: Which of these organisms commonly reproduces by budding?
questions.explanation: In Hydra, a bud develops as an outgrowth due to repeated cell division at one site, grows into a tiny individual and detaches. Amoeba reproduces by binary fission, Plasmodium by multiple fission and Planaria by regeneration.

questions.text: Mendel crossed pure tall (TT) pea plants with pure dwarf (tt) plants. What ratio of tall to dwarf plants appeared in the F₂ generation?
questions.explanation: All F₁ plants were tall (Tt). Self-pollinating them gives TT, Tt and tt in the ratio 1 : 2 : 1, so the ratio of tall to dwarf plants is 3 : 1.

questions.text: Producers in a food chain capture 10,000 J of energy. According to the 10% law, how much energy reaches the secondary consumers?
questions.explanation: Only about 10% of energy passes from one trophic level to the next: producers (10,000 J) → primary consumers (1,000 J) → secondary consumers (100 J).

questions.chapter: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
questions.text: Who is known as the architect of the unification of Germany?
questions.explanation: Otto von Bismarck, the chief minister of Prussia, led the process with the help of the Prussian army and bureaucracy. After three wars, Kaiser William I was proclaimed German Emperor at Versailles in January 1871.

questions.text: Why did Mahatma Gandhi choose salt to launch the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1930?
options: Salt was India's biggest export to Britain
Salt was the only commodity the British taxed
Salt-making was the main occupation in Gujarat
Salt was consumed by rich and poor alike, so a tax on it affected everyone
questions.explanation: Salt was an essential item of food for every Indian, and the salt tax and government monopoly over its production were widely resented. Breaking the salt law at Dandi on 6 April 1930 turned this shared grievance into a mass movement.

questions.chapter: The Making of a Global World
questions.text: What was rinderpest, which spread across Africa in the late 1880s?
options: A fast-spreading cattle plague that destroyed African livelihoods
A crop disease that wiped out wheat in the Sahara
A fever that affected only European soldiers
A pest that attacked rubber plantations
questions.explanation: Rinderpest was a cattle disease that entered Africa through infected cattle from British Asia and killed about 90 per cent of the cattle. The loss destroyed livelihoods and helped colonial powers force Africans into wage labour.

questions.text: Who was a 'gomastha' in the 18th-century Indian textile trade?
options: A wealthy Indian merchant who exported cloth
A weaver who owned his own loom
A paid servant of the East India Company who supervised weavers and checked cloth quality
A British factory inspector in Manchester
questions.explanation: To control the cloth trade directly, the East India Company appointed paid servants called gomasthas. They supervised weavers, collected supplies and examined the quality of cloth, and often treated weavers harshly.

questions.text: Which type of soil is best suited for growing cotton?
questions.explanation: Black soil, also called regur or black cotton soil, is made of fine clayey material and holds moisture well. This makes it ideal for cotton, especially on the Deccan plateau.

questions.text: Which Indian state was the first to make rooftop rainwater harvesting compulsory for all houses?
questions.explanation: Tamil Nadu made rooftop rainwater harvesting structures compulsory for all houses across the state, with legal provisions to punish defaulters. Rajasthan and Meghalaya are known for traditional harvesting systems instead.

questions.text: Which variety of coal is the highest quality hard coal?
questions.explanation: Anthracite has the highest carbon content and the least moisture, so it gives the most heat. Peat and lignite are low-grade coals, while bituminous coal is the most widely used commercially.

questions.text: The Golden Quadrilateral super highways connect which four cities?
questions.explanation: The Golden Quadrilateral links Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai and Mumbai with six-lane highways. Srinagar–Kanyakumari and Silchar–Porbandar are the North–South and East–West corridors.

questions.text: Belgium's 'community government', elected by people of one language community wherever they live, is an example of power sharing among:
questions.explanation: The community government represents the Dutch-, French- and German-speaking communities and handles cultural, educational and language matters. Sharing power among such linguistic or religious groups is power sharing among different social groups.

questions.text: Education, forests, trade unions, marriage, adoption and succession are subjects in which list of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Concurrent List has subjects of common interest to both the Union and the State governments. Both can make laws on them, but if the laws conflict, the law made by the Union Government prevails.

questions.text: What share of seats in local government bodies — panchayats and municipalities — is reserved for women in India?
questions.explanation: The Constitution reserves at least one-third of the seats in panchayats and municipalities for women. As a result, there are now more than 10 lakh elected women representatives in rural and urban local bodies.

questions.text: Under India's anti-defection law, what happens if an elected MLA or MP changes parties?
options: They lose their seat in the legislature
They must pay a fine to the Election Commission
They are banned from contesting elections for life
They lose only their right to vote in the House
questions.explanation: Defection means changing party allegiance after being elected from a particular party. The anti-defection law says such a legislator loses their seat, to stop members from switching parties for money or office.

questions.text: Which organisation publishes the Human Development Report, which compares countries on health, education and income?
questions.explanation: The UNDP's Human Development Report ranks countries on the Human Development Index, which combines life expectancy, education and per capita income. The World Bank, by contrast, classifies countries mainly by per capita income.

questions.text: What is meant by 'disguised unemployment'?
options: People who are actively searching for jobs but cannot find any
More people are working on a task than needed, so removing some would not reduce output
Workers who are unemployed during certain months of the year
Workers who hide their income to avoid paying taxes
questions.explanation: In disguised unemployment, people appear to be employed but are not really needed — for example, a whole family working on a small plot of land. If some members left, total production would stay the same. It is common in agriculture.

questions.text: Which of the following is a formal source of credit?
questions.explanation: Formal sources of credit, such as banks and cooperatives, are supervised by the Reserve Bank of India. Informal lenders like moneylenders and traders are unregulated and often charge much higher interest.

questions.text: Removing barriers or restrictions set by the government on trade and investment is known as:
questions.explanation: Liberalisation means removing government barriers such as import taxes and quotas. India began large-scale liberalisation in 1991, letting businesses trade and invest more freely.

questions.text: सूरदास के पद में गोपियाँ उद्धव को 'बड़भागी' कहती हैं। इसमें छिपा व्यंग्य क्या है?
options: उद्धव बहुत धनी और सुखी थे
उद्धव कृष्ण के पास रहकर भी उनके प्रेम से अछूते रहे
उद्धव को मथुरा का राजपाट मिल गया था
उद्धव ने गोपियों का दुख दूर कर दिया था
questions.explanation: गोपियाँ उद्धव की तुलना कमल के पत्ते और पानी में रखी तेल की गगरी से करती हैं, जिन पर पानी की बूँद नहीं ठहरती। वे कृष्ण के इतने निकट रहकर भी उनके प्रेम में नहीं बँधे — 'बड़भागी' कहना वास्तव में उनकी प्रेमहीनता पर व्यंग्य है।

questions.text: परशुराम के क्रोध का मुख्य कारण क्या था?
options: उन्हें सीता-स्वयंवर में नहीं बुलाया गया था
राम ने उन्हें प्रणाम नहीं किया था
राजा जनक ने उनका अपमान किया था
शिवजी का धनुष टूट गया था
questions.explanation: सीता-स्वयंवर में शिवजी का धनुष टूटने का समाचार सुनकर परशुराम क्रोधित होकर सभा में आए। शिव उनके आराध्य थे, इसलिए वे धनुष तोड़ने वाले को दंड देना चाहते थे।

questions.chapter: सूर्यकांत त्रिपाठी 'निराला' – उत्साह, अट नहीं रही है
questions.text: निराला की कविता 'अट नहीं रही है' में किस महीने की शोभा का वर्णन है?
questions.explanation: कविता की पहली पंक्ति है — 'अट नहीं रही है आभा फागुन की तन सट नहीं रही है।' फागुन की सुंदरता इतनी अधिक है कि वह कहीं समा नहीं पा रही और हर ओर बिखरी हुई है।

questions.text: 'संगतकार' कविता के अनुसार संगतकार अपनी आवाज़ को मुख्य गायक से ऊँचा क्यों नहीं उठने देता?
options: उसकी आवाज़ कमज़ोर और बेसुरी होती है
उसे राग का पूरा ज्ञान नहीं होता
वह मुख्य गायक के प्रति सम्मान के कारण ऐसा करता है
श्रोता उसकी आवाज़ पसंद नहीं करते
questions.explanation: संगतकार जानबूझकर अपना स्वर मुख्य गायक से नीचे रखता है ताकि मुख्य गायक की प्रतिष्ठा बनी रहे। कवि के अनुसार इसे उसकी विफलता नहीं, बल्कि उसकी मनुष्यता समझा जाना चाहिए।

questions.text: 'नेताजी का चश्मा' कहानी में नेताजी की मूर्ति पर बार-बार चश्मा कौन बदलता था?
questions.explanation: कस्बे का गरीब, देशभक्त चश्मेवाला, जिसे लोग 'कैप्टन' कहते थे, बिना चश्मे की मूर्ति देखकर दुखी होता था। कोई ग्राहक वैसा ही फ्रेम माँगता तो वह मूर्ति का चश्मा उतारकर उसे दे देता और मूर्ति पर दूसरा फ्रेम लगा देता था।

questions.text: 'लखनवी अंदाज़' में नवाब साहब ने अंत में खीरे की फाँकों के साथ क्या किया?
options: उन्हें बड़े चाव से खा लिया
उन्हें लेखक को खाने के लिए दे दिया
उन्हें घर ले जाने के लिए रूमाल में बाँध लिया
उन्हें सूँघकर एक-एक करके खिड़की से बाहर फेंक दिया
questions.explanation: नवाब साहब ने खीरे को बड़े सलीके से काटकर उस पर नमक-मिर्च बुरका, फिर हर फाँक को सूँघकर खिड़की से बाहर फेंक दिया। लेखक ने इसके माध्यम से नवाबों की दिखावटी, खोखली जीवन-शैली पर व्यंग्य किया है।

questions.text: शहनाई बजाने में प्रयुक्त 'रीड' किससे बनाई जाती है?
questions.explanation: पाठ के अनुसार रीड अंदर से पोली होती है और नरकट (एक प्रकार की घास) से बनाई जाती है, जो डुमराँव में मुख्यतः सोन नदी के किनारे मिलती है। इसी कारण शहनाई के लिए डुमराँव का महत्त्व बताया गया है।

questions.text: लेखक के अनुसार जिस योग्यता, प्रवृत्ति या प्रेरणा के बल पर कोई नया आविष्कार होता है, उसे क्या कहा जाता है?
questions.explanation: लेखक बताते हैं कि जिस योग्यता या प्रेरणा से आग या सुई-धागे जैसा आविष्कार हुआ, वह व्यक्ति की 'संस्कृति' है। उस संस्कृति से जो चीज़ बनी, यानी आविष्कार का परिणाम, वह 'सभ्यता' कहलाती है।

questions.text: 'माता का अँचल' पाठ में भोलानाथ का असली नाम क्या था?
questions.explanation: लेखक बताते हैं कि पिताजी उन्हें प्यार से 'भोलानाथ' कहकर पुकारते थे, पर उनका असली नाम तारकेश्वरनाथ था।

questions.text: 'साना-साना हाथ जोड़ि' यात्रा-वृत्तांत किस राज्य की यात्रा पर आधारित है?
questions.explanation: मधु कांकरिया का यह यात्रा-वृत्तांत सिक्किम की राजधानी गंगटोक और उससे आगे यूमथांग जैसी जगहों की यात्रा पर आधारित है। इसमें हिमालय के सौंदर्य के साथ वहाँ के लोगों के कठिन जीवन का भी चित्रण है।

questions.chapter: रचना के आधार पर वाक्य भेद
questions.text: 'जो छात्र परिश्रम करते हैं, वे सफल होते हैं।' — रचना के आधार पर यह वाक्य किस प्रकार का है?
questions.explanation: इस वाक्य में एक प्रधान उपवाक्य ('वे सफल होते हैं') और 'जो' से जुड़ा एक आश्रित उपवाक्य ('जो छात्र परिश्रम करते हैं') है। जिस वाक्य में प्रधान उपवाक्य के साथ आश्रित उपवाक्य हो, वह मिश्र वाक्य कहलाता है।

questions.text: 'राम द्वारा पत्र लिखा गया।' — यह वाक्य किस वाच्य में है?
questions.explanation: यहाँ क्रिया 'लिखा गया' कर्म 'पत्र' के लिंग-वचन के अनुसार है और कर्ता 'राम' के साथ 'द्वारा' लगा है। जब क्रिया कर्म के अनुसार हो, तो वाक्य कर्मवाच्य में होता है।

questions.text: 'वह तेज़ दौड़ता है।' — इस वाक्य में 'तेज़' पद का सही पद परिचय क्या है?
options: गुणवाचक विशेषण, 'वह' की विशेषता बताता है
रीतिवाचक क्रियाविशेषण, 'दौड़ता है' क्रिया की विशेषता बताता है
कालवाचक क्रियाविशेषण, 'दौड़ता है' क्रिया का समय बताता है
questions.explanation: 'तेज़' बताता है कि वह किस प्रकार दौड़ता है, इसलिए यह क्रिया की रीति (ढंग) बताने वाला रीतिवाचक क्रियाविशेषण है। 'तेज़ घोड़ा' जैसे प्रयोग में यही शब्द गुणवाचक विशेषण होता।

questions.text: हास्य रस का स्थायी भाव क्या है?
questions.explanation: हर रस का एक स्थायी भाव होता है: हास्य रस का 'हास', श्रृंगार रस का 'रति', वीर रस का 'उत्साह' और करुण रस का 'शोक'।

questions.text: In 'A Baker from Goa', what are the traditional bakers of Goa still known as?
questions.explanation: The bakers of Goa are still called pader, and the thud and jingle of their bamboo can still be heard in some places. 'Kabai' was the knee-length frock bakers once wore, and 'bol' is the sweet bread made for marriages.

questions.text: In which country did Gavin Maxwell get Mijbil, the otter?
questions.explanation: Early in 1956 Maxwell travelled to southern Iraq, where he got the otter cub that he named Mijbil. He later took it with him to London, which led to many adventures on the journey.

questions.text: In 'Madam Rides the Bus', what took away Valli's excitement on her journey back home?
options: The conductor scolded her for travelling alone
She lost the money she had saved for the ticket
The bus broke down far from her village
She saw the young cow she had laughed at earlier lying dead by the roadside
questions.explanation: On the way to town, Valli had laughed at a young cow running in front of the bus. On the way back she saw it lying dead by the roadside — her first encounter with death — and she lost her enthusiasm for the view outside.

questions.text: In Chekhov's 'The Proposal', what do Lomov and Natalya quarrel about?
options: The dowry and the date of the wedding
Who owns the Oxen Meadows and whose dog is better
Lomov's health and the size of his estate
A horse race and an unpaid debt
questions.explanation: Lomov comes to propose to Natalya, but they first argue over who owns the Oxen Meadows and later over whether his dog Guess or her family's dog Squeezer is better. Chekhov uses these petty quarrels to satirise marriages made for property.

questions.text: In Carl Sandburg's poem 'Fog', the fog is compared to which animal?
questions.explanation: Sandburg writes that the fog 'comes on little cat feet' and sits 'on silent haunches' before moving on. Like a cat, the fog arrives silently, stays for a while and leaves on its own.

questions.text: In 'Amanda!', why does Amanda imagine herself as a mermaid, an orphan and Rapunzel?
options: She wants to become an actress
She is bored of reading fairy tales
She wants to live by the sea
She longs to escape the constant nagging and instructions she receives
questions.explanation: Amanda is repeatedly told not to bite her nails, not to hunch her shoulders, to finish her homework and to avoid chocolates. Her daydreams of being a mermaid, an orphan or Rapunzel show how much she longs for freedom and peace.

questions.text: In 'A Triumph of Surgery', what was the real cause of Tricki's illness?
options: A rare infection caught from another dog
An injury from a road accident
Poisonous food eaten in the garden
questions.explanation: Mrs Pumphrey pampered Tricki with too much rich food and too little exercise, so he became fat and listless. Dr Herriot cured him without any medicine, using a strict diet and plenty of play with other dogs at his surgery.

questions.text: What shocking truth does Matilda Loisel learn at the end of 'The Necklace'?
options: Mme Forestier had found the lost necklace long ago
The necklace she lost was made of false diamonds worth very little
Mme Forestier had planned to give her the necklace as a gift
The jeweller had cheated them while selling the replacement
questions.explanation: After ten years of hard work to repay the 36,000 francs spent on a replacement, Matilda learns that Mme Forestier's necklace was fake and worth at most 500 francs. The ending shows how vanity and the fear of admitting a mistake cost her years of her life.

questions.text: Choose the correct determiner: I did not have ____ money left to buy the book.
questions.explanation: 'Money' is an uncountable noun, so it takes 'much', especially in negative sentences and questions. 'Many', 'few' and 'a few' are used only with countable nouns such as 'books' or 'coins'.

questions.text: Which of the following is the prime factorisation of 3825?
questions.explanation: Dividing by primes: 3825 = 3 × 1275 = 3 × 3 × 425 = 3² × 5 × 85 = 3² × 5 × 5 × 17, so 3825 = 3² × 5² × 17. Products containing 51 or 85 also equal 3825, but they are not prime factorisations because 51 = 3 × 17 and 85 = 5 × 17.

questions.text: If 2 is a zero of the polynomial p(x) = x² + 3x + k, what is the value of k?
questions.explanation: If 2 is a zero, then p(2) = 0: 2² + 3(2) + k = 4 + 6 + k = 0, so k = −10.

questions.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
questions.text: Half the perimeter of a rectangular garden is 36 m, and its length is 4 m more than its width. What is the length of the garden?
questions.explanation: Let the length be l and the width w. Then l + w = 36 and l − w = 4. Adding the two equations gives 2l = 40, so l = 20 m (and w = 16 m).

questions.text: A vertical pole 6 m long casts a shadow 4 m long on the ground. At the same time, a tower casts a shadow 28 m long. What is the height of the tower?
questions.explanation: At the same time the sun's rays make the same angle with the ground, so the pole and the tower form similar triangles with their shadows. Then 6/4 = h/28, so h = 42 m.

questions.text: From an external point T, two tangents TP and TQ are drawn to a circle with centre O. If ∠PTQ = 70°, what is ∠POQ?
questions.explanation: The radius is perpendicular to the tangent, so ∠OPT = ∠OQT = 90°. The angles of quadrilateral OPTQ add up to 360°, so ∠POQ = 360° − 90° − 90° − 70° = 110°.

questions.text: A kite is flying at a height of 60 m above the ground. Its string, assumed to be tight, makes an angle of 60° with the ground. What is the length of the string?
questions.explanation: sin 60° = height ÷ length of string, so √3/2 = 60/L. Then L = 120/√3 = 40√3 m (about 69.3 m).

questions.text: A chord of a circle of radius 10 cm subtends a right angle at the centre. What is the area of the minor segment? (Use π = 3.14)
questions.explanation: Area of the minor sector = (90/360) × 3.14 × 10² = 78.5 cm². Subtracting the right triangle formed by the two radii, (1/2) × 10 × 10 = 50 cm², gives the minor segment: 78.5 − 50 = 28.5 cm².

questions.text: A solid is in the shape of a cone standing on a hemisphere, both of radius 1 cm, and the height of the cone is equal to its radius. What is the volume of the solid?
questions.explanation: Volume of the cone = (1/3)πr²h = (1/3)π(1)²(1) = π/3 cm³, and volume of the hemisphere = (2/3)πr³ = 2π/3 cm³. Total volume = π/3 + 2π/3 = π cm³.

questions.text: What is the class mark of the class interval 10–25?
questions.explanation: The class mark is the midpoint of a class: (upper limit + lower limit) ÷ 2 = (10 + 25) ÷ 2 = 17.5. Class marks represent each class when finding the mean of grouped data.

questions.text: A bag contains 3 red balls and 5 black balls. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is NOT red?
questions.explanation: There are 3 + 5 = 8 balls, and 5 of them are not red, so P(not red) = 5/8. This also equals 1 − P(red) = 1 − 3/8.

questions.text: What is the nature of the magnetic field inside a long, straight, current-carrying solenoid?
options: It is uniform, shown by parallel straight field lines
It is strongest near the walls and zero along the axis
It forms circles around the axis of the solenoid
questions.explanation: Inside a long solenoid the field lines are parallel straight lines, which means the magnetic field is the same at all points — a uniform field. Placing a soft iron core inside such a coil makes an electromagnet.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of the earth wire in a domestic electric circuit?
options: It carries the main current to all appliances
It raises the voltage supplied to heavy appliances
It stores extra charge for use during power cuts
It gives leakage current a low-resistance path to the ground, protecting users from shocks
questions.explanation: The earth wire connects the metal body of an appliance to the ground. If the body accidentally becomes live, the current flows safely to the earth instead of through the person touching it.

questions.text: The refractive index of glass is 1.5. What is the speed of light in glass? (Speed of light in vacuum = 3 × 10⁸ m/s)
questions.explanation: Refractive index n = speed of light in vacuum ÷ speed of light in the medium. So v = c/n = (3 × 10⁸) ÷ 1.5 = 2 × 10⁸ m/s — light slows down in an optically denser medium.

questions.text: The resistivity of a metallic wire depends on which of the following?
options: The nature of the material and its temperature
The area of cross-section of the wire
The current flowing through the wire
questions.explanation: Resistance depends on a wire's length and area of cross-section, but resistivity (ρ in R = ρl/A) is a property of the material itself. It changes only with the nature of the material and its temperature, not with the wire's dimensions.

questions.text: Which of the following metal oxides is amphoteric, reacting with both acids and bases?
questions.explanation: Aluminium oxide reacts with acids (forming salts such as AlCl₃) and with bases (forming sodium aluminate), so it is amphoteric. Zinc oxide behaves the same way, while sodium, magnesium and calcium oxides are basic.

questions.text: Which conditions are needed for iron to rust?
questions.explanation: Iron nails rust only when exposed to both air and water — not in boiled water sealed under oil, and not in dry air kept over anhydrous calcium chloride. Painting, oiling or galvanising prevents rusting by keeping air and moisture away.

questions.text: When lead nitrate is heated, brown fumes are given off. Which gas produces these fumes?
questions.explanation: On heating, lead nitrate decomposes: 2Pb(NO₃)₂ → 2PbO + 4NO₂ + O₂. Oxygen is colourless; the brown fumes are nitrogen dioxide. This is a thermal decomposition reaction.

questions.text: When soap cleans an oily stain, its molecules form micelles. How are the soap molecules arranged in a micelle?
options: Ionic ends point inward towards the oil, and carbon chains face the water
Carbon chains point inward into the oil, and ionic ends face the water
All the soap molecules lie flat on the surface of the cloth
The soap molecules react chemically with the oil and destroy it
questions.explanation: A soap molecule has a hydrocarbon tail that dissolves in oil and an ionic head that dissolves in water. In a micelle the tails cluster around the oily dirt at the centre while the ionic heads face outward into the water, so the dirt can be rinsed away.

questions.text: What is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of a flower called?
questions.explanation: The transfer of pollen from the anther to the stigma is pollination — self-pollination within the same flower, cross-pollination between flowers of different plants. Fertilisation happens later, when the male germ cell fuses with the female germ cell in the ovule.

questions.text: In human females, where does fertilisation of the egg normally take place?
questions.explanation: Sperms travel up to the oviduct, where they may meet the egg released by the ovary, and fertilisation takes place there. The fertilised egg (zygote) then moves down and gets implanted in the lining of the uterus.

questions.text: In humans, what determines whether a baby will be a boy or a girl?
options: Whether the father's sperm carries an X or a Y chromosome
Whether the mother's egg carries an X or a Y chromosome
The temperature at which the baby develops
questions.explanation: Women have two X chromosomes, so every egg carries an X. Men have one X and one Y, so a sperm can carry either. A child who inherits an X from the father is a girl (XX), and one who inherits a Y is a boy (XY).

questions.text: In the food chain grass → grasshopper → frog → snake, a non-biodegradable pesticide gets into the grass. Which organism will have the highest concentration of the pesticide?
questions.explanation: Non-biodegradable chemicals are not broken down, so they accumulate at each trophic level. This biological magnification makes their concentration highest in the top consumer — here, the snake.

questions.chapter: Print Culture and the Modern World
questions.text: Who wrote the 'Ninety Five Theses' in 1517, criticising practices of the Roman Catholic Church — a text that spread widely thanks to print?
questions.explanation: Martin Luther's Ninety Five Theses were printed in large numbers and read widely, leading to the Protestant Reformation. Deeply indebted to print, Luther called printing 'the ultimate gift of God and the greatest one'.

questions.text: In which year was Project Tiger launched in India?
questions.explanation: Project Tiger was launched in 1973, when the tiger population had fallen sharply because of poaching and shrinking habitats. Reserves such as Corbett, Sundarbans and Bandhavgarh are part of it.

questions.text: Rabi crops are sown in winter and harvested in summer. Which of these is a rabi crop?
questions.explanation: Wheat, barley, peas, gram and mustard are important rabi crops, sown from October to December and harvested from April to June. Paddy, cotton and jute are kharif crops, sown with the onset of the monsoon.

questions.text: Which industry is called a 'basic industry' because all other industries depend on it for their machinery?
questions.explanation: Heavy, medium and light industries all depend on machinery made of iron and steel, so the iron and steel industry is called a basic industry. It is also a heavy industry, because its raw materials and finished goods are heavy and bulky.

questions.text: According to the chapter 'Outcomes of Democracy', what is the most basic outcome that democracy should produce?
options: A government that is accountable, responsive and legitimate
Rapid economic growth in every democratic country
Complete economic equality among all citizens
Quick decisions taken without long debates
questions.explanation: Democracy's most basic outcome is a government that is accountable to citizens, responsive to their needs and legitimate because the people elect it. Democracies may take longer to decide, and they do not guarantee faster growth or an end to inequality.

questions.text: Which incident made Mahatma Gandhi call off the Non-Cooperation Movement in February 1922?
options: The violent clash at Chauri Chaura
The arrival of the Simon Commission
The failure of the Second Round Table Conference
questions.explanation: At Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur, a peaceful demonstration turned into a violent clash with the police. Gandhiji felt the movement was turning violent and that satyagrahis needed proper training first, so he withdrew it.

questions.text: India, Spain and Belgium are examples of which kind of federation?
options: 'Coming together' federations formed by independent states
Unitary states with no division of power
'Holding together' federations, where a large country divides power among its parts
questions.explanation: In a 'holding together' federation, a large country decides to divide power between the central government and its states, and the centre tends to be more powerful. In 'coming together' federations like the USA, Switzerland and Australia, independent states joined to form a bigger unit.

questions.text: By 2013-14, which sector had emerged as the largest producing sector in India in terms of GDP?
questions.explanation: Between 1973-74 and 2013-14, production grew the most in the tertiary sector, which replaced the primary sector as the largest producing sector. However, more than half of India's workers are still employed in the primary sector.

questions.text: 'आत्मकथ्य' कविता में जयशंकर प्रसाद अपनी आत्मकथा लिखने से क्यों बचना चाहते हैं?
options: उनके पास लिखने के लिए समय नहीं था
प्रकाशक ने उनकी आत्मकथा छापने से मना कर दिया था
वे केवल नाटक लिखना पसंद करते थे
वे अपने जीवन को साधारण मानते थे और अपनी निजी व्यथाएँ उजागर नहीं करना चाहते थे
questions.explanation: कवि को लगता है कि उनका जीवन सीधा-सादा है और उसमें दूसरों को सुनाने लायक कोई बड़ी उपलब्धि नहीं है — 'छोटे से जीवन की कैसे बड़ी कथाएँ आज कहूँ?' वे अपनी मधुर स्मृतियों और दुखों को भी सबके सामने नहीं खोलना चाहते।

questions.text: नागार्जुन की कविता 'यह दंतुरित मुसकान' में 'दंतुरित मुसकान' किसकी है?
options: नए-नए दाँतों वाले छोटे बच्चे की
questions.explanation: 'दंतुरित' का अर्थ है जिसके नए-नए दाँत निकल रहे हों। कवि छोटे बच्चे की इस मुसकान को इतना मोहक बताते हैं कि वह मृतक में भी जान डाल दे — 'तुम्हारी यह दंतुरित मुसकान / मृतक में भी डाल देगी जान'।

questions.text: बालगोबिन भगत किस संत को 'साहब' मानते थे और उन्हीं के गीत गाते थे?
questions.explanation: बालगोबिन भगत कबीर को 'साहब' मानते थे, उन्हीं के गीतों को गाते और उन्हीं के आदेशों पर चलते थे। गृहस्थ होते हुए भी उनका जीवन संतों जैसा सरल और सच्चा था।

questions.chapter: मन्नू भंडारी – एक कहानी यह भी
questions.text: 'एक कहानी यह भी' में लेखिका के व्यक्तित्व और सोच पर किस अध्यापिका का गहरा प्रभाव पड़ा?
questions.explanation: हिंदी की प्राध्यापिका शीला अग्रवाल ने लेखिका को अच्छा साहित्य चुनकर पढ़ने और उस पर बहस करने के लिए प्रेरित किया। उन्हीं के प्रभाव से लेखिका स्वतंत्रता आंदोलन की गतिविधियों में भी सक्रिय रूप से भाग लेने लगीं।

questions.text: 'मैं क्यों लिखता हूँ?' में अज्ञेय ने 'हिरोशिमा' कविता किस अनुभव के बाद लिखी?
options: हिरोशिमा में एक जले हुए पत्थर पर मनुष्य की उजली छाया देखकर
अखबार में युद्ध की खबर पढ़कर
एक जापानी कवि से भेंट करके
किसी फ़िल्म में बमबारी के दृश्य देखकर
questions.explanation: हिरोशिमा में लेखक ने एक जले हुए पत्थर पर एक लंबी उजली छाया देखी — विस्फोट के समय वहाँ खड़ा मनुष्य भाप बनकर उड़ गया था। इस अनुभूति ने उन्हें भीतर तक झकझोर दिया, और भारत लौटकर रेलगाड़ी में बैठे-बैठे उन्होंने 'हिरोशिमा' कविता लिखी।

questions.text: 'आँखें बिछाना' मुहावरे का सही अर्थ क्या है?
questions.explanation: 'आँखें बिछाना' का अर्थ है किसी के आने पर बहुत प्रेम और उत्साह से उसका स्वागत करना। उदाहरण: छुट्टियों में आए नाती-पोतों के स्वागत में नाना-नानी ने आँखें बिछा दीं।

questions.text: What is the dimensional formula of force?
questions.explanation: Force = mass × acceleration, and acceleration has dimensions [LT⁻²]. So force has dimensions [M] × [LT⁻²] = [MLT⁻²].

questions.text: A ball is dropped from rest from a height of 20 m. Taking g = 10 m/s², how long does it take to reach the ground?
questions.explanation: With zero initial velocity, h = ½gt². So 20 = ½ × 10 × t², giving t² = 4 and t = 2 s.

questions.text: A net force of 10 N acts on a body of mass 2 kg. What is the acceleration of the body?
questions.explanation: Newton's second law gives F = ma, so a = F/m = 10 N ÷ 2 kg = 5 m/s².

questions.text: A body of mass 2 kg is moving with a speed of 3 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy K = ½mv² = ½ × 2 kg × (3 m/s)² = 9 J. Forgetting the factor ½ is the most common mistake here.

questions.text: If the distance between two point masses is doubled, the gravitational force between them becomes:
questions.explanation: By Newton's law of gravitation, F = Gm₁m₂/r², so F ∝ 1/r². Doubling r makes the force 1/2² = 1/4 of its original value.

questions.text: In an isothermal process involving an ideal gas, which of these quantities remains constant?
questions.explanation: Isothermal means 'at constant temperature'. Pressure, volume and density can all change, but since the internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature, ΔU = 0 in this process.

questions.text: At a certain temperature the rms speed of oxygen (O₂) molecules is v. What is the rms speed of hydrogen (H₂) molecules at the same temperature?
questions.explanation: v_rms = √(3RT/M), so at the same temperature v_rms ∝ 1/√M. Hence v(H₂)/v(O₂) = √(32/2) = √16 = 4, so the rms speed of hydrogen is 4v.

questions.text: How many moles of water are present in 36 g of H₂O? (Molar mass of H₂O = 18 g/mol)
questions.explanation: Number of moles = mass ÷ molar mass = 36 g ÷ 18 g/mol = 2 mol.

questions.text: What is the maximum number of electrons that can be accommodated in the shell with principal quantum number n = 3?
questions.explanation: A shell can hold at most 2n² electrons. For n = 3 this is 2 × 3² = 18 (2 in 3s, 6 in 3p and 10 in 3d).

questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Which of the following elements has the highest electronegativity?
questions.explanation: Electronegativity increases across a period and decreases down a group. Fluorine is the most electronegative element (4.0 on the Pauling scale).

questions.text: What is the shape of the methane (CH₄) molecule?
questions.explanation: Carbon in CH₄ is sp³ hybridised with four bond pairs and no lone pairs, so the molecule is tetrahedral with H–C–H bond angles of about 109.5°.

questions.text: What is the pH of a 0.001 M solution of HCl at 25 °C?
questions.explanation: HCl is a strong acid and ionises completely, so [H⁺] = 10⁻³ M. pH = −log[H⁺] = −log(10⁻³) = 3.

questions.text: What is the oxidation number of chromium in potassium dichromate, K₂Cr₂O₇?
questions.explanation: Let the oxidation number of Cr be x. Then 2(+1) + 2x + 7(−2) = 0, so 2x = 12 and x = +6.

questions.text: What is the major product when HBr is added to propene (CH₃–CH=CH₂) in the absence of peroxide?
questions.explanation: Without peroxide, HBr adds according to Markovnikov's rule: H⁺ attaches to the carbon with more hydrogens, forming the more stable secondary carbocation, so Br⁻ bonds to C-2 to give 2-bromopropane.

questions.text: If A = {1, 2, 3} and B = {3, 4}, then A ∪ B is:
questions.explanation: The union A ∪ B contains every element that belongs to A or to B (or both), each listed once: {1, 2, 3, 4}.

questions.text: What is the value of sin 30° · cos 60° + cos 30° · sin 60°?
questions.explanation: sin A cos B + cos A sin B = sin(A + B) = sin 90° = 1. Directly: (1/2)(1/2) + (√3/2)(√3/2) = 1/4 + 3/4 = 1.

questions.text: What is the value of i⁴¹, where i = √−1?
questions.explanation: Powers of i repeat in a cycle of 4: i, −1, −i, 1. Since 41 = 4 × 10 + 1, i⁴¹ = i¹ = i.

questions.text: In how many different ways can the letters of the word APPLE be arranged?
questions.explanation: APPLE has 5 letters in which P occurs twice, so the number of distinct arrangements is 5!/2! = 120/2 = 60.

questions.text: What is the sum of the infinite geometric series 1 + 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + … ?
questions.explanation: Here a = 1 and r = 1/2. Since |r| < 1, the sum to infinity is a/(1 − r) = 1/(1 − 1/2) = 2.

questions.text: What is the slope of the line 2x + 3y − 6 = 0?
questions.explanation: Rewriting the equation as y = −(2/3)x + 2 shows the slope is −2/3. In general, the line ax + by + c = 0 has slope −a/b.

questions.text: What is the value of lim (x → 0) of (1 − cos x)/x² ?
questions.explanation: Use 1 − cos x = 2 sin²(x/2). The limit becomes lim 2 sin²(x/2)/x² = (2/4) × [sin(x/2)/(x/2)]² → (1/2) × 1 = 1/2.

questions.text: Who proposed the system of binomial nomenclature for naming organisms?
questions.explanation: Carolus Linnaeus introduced binomial nomenclature, in which every organism gets a two-part scientific name: a generic name followed by a specific epithet (e.g. Mangifera indica).

questions.text: Which cell organelle is known as the 'powerhouse of the cell'?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are the sites of aerobic respiration and produce most of the cell's energy in the form of ATP, which is why they are called the powerhouse of the cell.

questions.text: In Whittaker's five-kingdom classification, bacteria are placed in which kingdom?
questions.explanation: R.H. Whittaker (1969) placed all prokaryotic organisms, including bacteria, in Kingdom Monera.

questions.text: During which stage of meiosis does crossing over take place?
questions.explanation: Crossing over — the exchange of segments between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes — occurs during pachytene of prophase I, after the homologues have paired in zygotene.

questions.text: In C₄ plants, what is the first stable product of carbon dioxide fixation?
questions.explanation: In the mesophyll cells of C₄ plants, PEP carboxylase fixes CO₂ with phosphoenolpyruvate to form oxaloacetic acid, a 4-carbon compound — which is why these plants are called C₄ plants.

questions.text: Which chamber of the human heart pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta?
questions.explanation: Oxygenated blood from the lungs enters the left atrium, passes to the left ventricle, and the thick-walled left ventricle pumps it into the aorta for the whole body.

questions.text: Which hormone is secreted by the pars intermedia of the pituitary gland?
questions.explanation: The pars intermedia secretes only melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH). Prolactin and TSH come from the pars distalis, while oxytocin is released from the posterior pituitary (pars nervosa).

questions.text: Two point charges exert a force F on each other when they are a distance r apart. If the distance between them is doubled, the force becomes:
questions.explanation: Coulomb's force varies inversely as the square of the distance (F ∝ 1/r²). Doubling r makes the force 1/2² = 1/4 of its original value.

questions.text: Two capacitors of 3 μF and 6 μF are connected in series. The equivalent capacitance of the combination is:
questions.explanation: For capacitors in series, 1/C = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂ = 1/3 + 1/6 = 1/2, so C = 2 μF. A series combination is always smaller than the smallest capacitor.

questions.text: A wire of resistance R is stretched uniformly to twice its original length while its volume remains constant. Its new resistance is:
questions.explanation: With constant volume, doubling the length halves the cross-sectional area. Since R = ρL/A, the resistance increases by a factor of 2 × 2 = 4.

questions.text: A charged particle moves with velocity v parallel to a uniform magnetic field B. The magnetic force acting on it is:
questions.explanation: The magnetic force is F = qvB sin θ. For motion parallel to the field, θ = 0° and sin 0° = 0, so no magnetic force acts on the particle.

questions.text: The magnetic flux through each turn of a 100-turn coil changes from 5 × 10⁻³ Wb to 1 × 10⁻³ Wb in 0.02 s. The magnitude of the average induced emf is:
questions.explanation: By Faraday's law, |ε| = N·ΔΦ/Δt = 100 × (4 × 10⁻³ Wb)/(0.02 s) = 20 V.

questions.text: A convex lens of focal length 20 cm is placed in contact with a concave lens of focal length 40 cm. The power of the combination is:
questions.explanation: Powers of lenses in contact add: P = 1/(0.20 m) + 1/(−0.40 m) = 5 D − 2.5 D = +2.5 D, so the combination acts as a converging lens of focal length 40 cm.

questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.text: An electron is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 100 V. Its de Broglie wavelength is approximately:
questions.explanation: For an electron accelerated through V volts, λ = h/√(2meV) ≈ 1.227/√V nm. With V = 100 V, λ ≈ 1.227/10 ≈ 0.123 nm.

questions.text: Which of the following is a colligative property of a dilute solution?
questions.explanation: Colligative properties depend only on the number of solute particles, not their nature. Osmotic pressure is one, along with relative lowering of vapour pressure, elevation of boiling point and depression of freezing point.

questions.text: Given limiting molar conductivities (in S cm² mol⁻¹): HCl = 426.2, NaCl = 126.5 and CH₃COONa = 91.0. Using Kohlrausch's law, the limiting molar conductivity of CH₃COOH is:
questions.explanation: By Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions, Λ°(CH₃COOH) = Λ°(CH₃COONa) + Λ°(HCl) − Λ°(NaCl) = 91.0 + 426.2 − 126.5 = 390.7 S cm² mol⁻¹.

questions.text: A first-order reaction has a rate constant of 0.0693 min⁻¹. Its half-life is:
questions.explanation: For a first-order reaction, t½ = 0.693/k = 0.693/0.0693 min⁻¹ = 10 min. The half-life does not depend on the initial concentration.

questions.text: The steady decrease in atomic and ionic radii from lanthanum to lutetium is known as:
questions.explanation: 4f electrons shield the outer electrons poorly, so the effective nuclear charge rises across the series and the radii shrink steadily. This is called the lanthanoid contraction.

questions.text: In K₄[Fe(CN)₆], the oxidation state and the coordination number of iron are respectively:
questions.explanation: The complex ion [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻ carries a −4 charge; with six CN⁻ ligands (−1 each), x − 6 = −4 gives Fe = +2. Six monodentate ligands make the coordination number 6.

questions.text: Which of the following alkyl halides reacts fastest by the SN2 mechanism?
questions.explanation: SN2 involves backside attack by the nucleophile, so bulky groups around the carbon slow it down. Reactivity follows methyl > primary > secondary > tertiary, making CH₃Br the fastest.

questions.text: Which of the following is the strongest base in aqueous solution?
questions.explanation: Electron-donating alkyl groups and good solvation make aliphatic amines stronger bases than NH₃; in water, dimethylamine (pKb ≈ 3.27) is the strongest here. Aniline is the weakest because its lone pair is delocalised into the benzene ring.

questions.text: The function f : R → R defined by f(x) = 2x + 3 is:
questions.explanation: f(x₁) = f(x₂) gives 2x₁ + 3 = 2x₂ + 3, so x₁ = x₂ (one-one). Every real y has the pre-image (y − 3)/2 (onto), so f is a bijection.

questions.text: The principal value of sin⁻¹(−1/2) is:
questions.explanation: The principal value branch of sin⁻¹ is [−π/2, π/2]. Since sin(−π/6) = −1/2 and −π/6 lies in this interval, sin⁻¹(−1/2) = −π/6.

questions.text: If A is a square matrix of order 3 and |A| = 5, then |2A| equals:
questions.explanation: Multiplying an n × n matrix by k multiplies every row by k, so |kA| = kⁿ|A|. Here |2A| = 2³ × 5 = 40.

questions.text: If A is a matrix of order 2 × 3 and B is a matrix of order 3 × 4, then the order of the product AB is:
questions.explanation: AB is defined because the number of columns of A equals the number of rows of B (3). The product has the rows of A and the columns of B, so its order is 2 × 4.

questions.text: If y = e^(sin x), then dy/dx equals:
questions.explanation: By the chain rule, d/dx(eᵘ) = eᵘ · du/dx. With u = sin x and du/dx = cos x, the derivative is e^(sin x) · cos x.

questions.text: The value of the definite integral of sin²x from x = 0 to x = π/2 is:
questions.explanation: Using sin²x = (1 − cos 2x)/2, the integral equals [x/2 − (sin 2x)/4] from 0 to π/2 = π/4 − 0 = π/4.

questions.text: Bag I contains 3 red and 4 black balls; Bag II contains 5 red and 6 black balls. A bag is chosen at random and a ball drawn from it is found to be red. The probability that it was drawn from Bag II is:
In flowering plants, the triploid primary endosperm nucleus is formed by the fusion of:
options: A male gamete with the two polar nuclei
A male gamete with the egg cell
The egg cell with a synergid
Two male gametes with each other
questions.explanation: In double fertilisation, one male gamete fuses with the egg (syngamy) and the other fuses with the two polar nuclei (triple fusion), forming the triploid (3n) primary endosperm nucleus.

questions.text: Which hormone's mid-cycle surge induces ovulation in the human menstrual cycle?
questions.explanation: Around the middle of the cycle (about day 14), a rapid rise in LH (the LH surge) causes the mature Graafian follicle to rupture and release the secondary oocyte.

questions.text: When two pea plants heterozygous for both seed shape and seed colour (RrYy × RrYy) are crossed, the F2 phenotypic ratio is:
questions.explanation: The two gene pairs assort independently, giving 9 plants with both dominant traits, 3 and 3 with one dominant trait each, and 1 with both recessive traits — a 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 ratio.

questions.text: A double-stranded DNA sample contains 20% adenine. What percentage of its bases is cytosine?
questions.explanation: By Chargaff's rule, A = T and G = C. So A + T = 40%, leaving G + C = 60%, which means cytosine = 30%.

questions.text: Malaria is caused by:
questions.explanation: Malaria is caused by protozoans of the genus Plasmodium (such as P. vivax and P. falciparum) and is spread by the bite of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.

questions.text: Which palindromic DNA sequence is recognised and cut by the restriction enzyme EcoRI?
questions.explanation: EcoRI recognises the palindrome 5′-GAATTC-3′ and cuts between G and A on both strands, leaving sticky ends. GGATCC and AAGCTT are recognised by BamHI and HindIII respectively.

questions.text: According to Lindeman's 10 per cent law, if the producers in a food chain fix 10,000 J of energy, the energy available to the secondary consumers is about:
questions.explanation: Only about 10% of the energy passes to each higher trophic level: 10,000 J (producers) → 1,000 J (primary consumers) → 100 J (secondary consumers).

questions.text: In 'The Portrait of a Lady', after the author went to university, how did his grandmother spend half an hour every afternoon?
options: Feeding the sparrows in the courtyard
Teaching the village children to read
Feeding the stray dogs near the temple
Reading the scriptures aloud to neighbours
questions.explanation: Left alone in the city, the grandmother accepted her seclusion; she spun at her wheel and relaxed each afternoon by feeding the sparrows, who gathered around her in large numbers. Feeding stray dogs belonged to her village days.

questions.text: In 'Discovering Tut: the Saga Continues', what was used in 2005 to examine Tutankhamun's mummy in detail?
options: An X-ray machine brought from Cairo University
A carbon-dating laboratory set up in the tomb
questions.explanation: In January 2005 a team led by Zahi Hawass used a portable CT (computed tomography) scanner, brought to the Valley of the Kings in a trailer, to build a detailed 3-D image of the mummy and investigate how Tut lived and died.

questions.chapter: The Summer of the Beautiful White Horse
questions.text: Why did Mourad and Aram finally return the white horse to John Byro?
options: John Byro offered them a reward for it
Uncle Khosrove ordered them to give it back
Their family's famous honesty made them unwilling to keep it
The horse fell ill and could no longer be ridden
questions.explanation: When John Byro saw the horse he said he would swear it was his, but he trusted the Garoghlanian family's well-known reputation for honesty. The boys could not betray that reputation, so they returned the horse early the next morning.

questions.text: In 'The Address', why does the narrator decide to forget the address at Marconi Street without taking back her mother's belongings?
options: Mrs Dorling's daughter threatened to call the police
Her mother had asked her never to go back there
The house had been demolished after the war
Cut off from the life they once belonged to, the objects had lost their meaning for her
questions.explanation: Seeing her mother's things in a stranger's room, the narrator feels they no longer connect her to the past she loved. Their value lay in the life they were part of, so she chooses to leave them and forget the address.

questions.text: Choose the correct option to complete the sentence: 'By the time we reached the station, the train ____.'
questions.explanation: When one past action happened before another past action, the earlier one takes the past perfect (had + past participle). The train left before we reached, so 'had left' is correct.

questions.text: In 'The Last Lesson', why was M. Hamel wearing his fine green coat and frilled shirt that day?
options: It was his last French lesson, as orders from Berlin allowed only German to be taught
A school inspector was visiting the class that morning
It was the day of the annual prize distribution
The mayor had invited him to a ceremony after school
questions.explanation: Orders had come from Berlin that only German would be taught in the schools of Alsace and Lorraine. M. Hamel dressed in his best clothes, usually kept for inspection and prize days, to honour the last French lesson.

questions.text: In 'Lost Spring', Saheb-e-Alam's family had migrated to Seemapuri from which country?
questions.explanation: Saheb's family came from Dhaka, Bangladesh, in 1971 after storms swept away their fields and homes. Like many migrants in Seemapuri, they survived by ragpicking.

questions.text: In 'Deep Water', how did William O. Douglas finally overcome his fear of water?
options: He forced himself to jump off the diving board every day
He joined a summer camp for swimmers in the mountains
An instructor trained him bit by bit, holding him with a rope and pulley in the pool
He read books on swimming and practised the strokes on land
questions.explanation: Douglas hired an instructor who taught him swimming piece by piece: a belt around his waist was attached to a rope running through a pulley, so he could practise without panic. Months of this training, followed by swimming alone, conquered his terror.

questions.text: In 'Keeping Quiet', what does Pablo Neruda ask everyone to do while he counts to twelve?
options: Remember the soldiers who died in wars
Plant a tree for the earth
Keep still and stop all activity for a moment
questions.explanation: The poet asks all of us to count to twelve and keep still, without talking or moving. In that moment of silence and introspection, people could understand themselves and stop harming one another and the earth.

questions.text: In 'The Rattrap', what made the peddler return the thirty kronor he had stolen from the old crofter?
options: The ironmaster threatened to hand him over to the police
Edla Willmansson's kindness and respect made him want to act like a captain
The crofter caught up with him on the road
He found more money hidden in the manor house
questions.explanation: Edla treated the peddler with compassion and dignity even after learning he was not Captain von Ståhle. Her kindness awakened his goodness, so he left the stolen money in a rattrap as a Christmas present and signed himself as a captain.

questions.text: काव्यशास्त्र में रस के कितने अंग माने गए हैं?
questions.explanation: रस के चार अंग होते हैं — स्थायी भाव, विभाव, अनुभाव और संचारी (व्यभिचारी) भाव। इन्हीं के संयोग से रस की निष्पत्ति होती है; 'नौ' रसों की संख्या है, अंगों की नहीं।

questions.text: 'चरण कमल बंदौं हरि राई' — इस पंक्ति में कौन-सा अलंकार है?
questions.explanation: यहाँ उपमेय 'चरण' और उपमान 'कमल' में भेद नहीं किया गया, बल्कि चरणों को ही कमल मान लिया गया है। उपमेय पर उपमान का ऐसा अभेद आरोप रूपक अलंकार कहलाता है।

questions.text: 'विद्यालय' शब्द में कौन-सी संधि है?
questions.explanation: विद्यालय = विद्या + आलय। जब दो सजातीय स्वर (आ + आ) मिलकर दीर्घ 'आ' बनाते हैं, तो उसे दीर्घ संधि कहते हैं।

questions.text: 'यथाशक्ति' शब्द में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.explanation: यथाशक्ति का विग्रह है 'शक्ति के अनुसार'। इसका पहला पद 'यथा' अव्यय है और पूरा पद क्रियाविशेषण की तरह प्रयुक्त होता है, इसलिए यह अव्ययीभाव समास है।

questions.text: दोहा छंद के विषम और सम चरणों में क्रमशः कितनी मात्राएँ होती हैं?
questions.explanation: दोहा एक अर्धसम मात्रिक छंद है: विषम (पहले और तीसरे) चरणों में 13-13 तथा सम (दूसरे और चौथे) चरणों में 11-11 मात्राएँ होती हैं। इसका उल्टा क्रम (11 और 13) सोरठा का होता है।

questions.text: वीर रस का स्थायी भाव क्या है?
questions.explanation: वीर रस का स्थायी भाव उत्साह है। क्रोध रौद्र रस का, भय भयानक रस का और रति शृंगार रस का स्थायी भाव है।

questions.text: 'काली घटा का घमंड घटा' — इस पंक्ति में कौन-सा अलंकार है?
questions.explanation: यहाँ 'घटा' शब्द दो बार आया है और दोनों बार अर्थ अलग है — पहला 'बादलों की घटा' और दूसरा 'कम हो गया'। एक ही शब्द का अलग-अलग अर्थों में बार-बार आना यमक अलंकार है; श्लेष में शब्द एक ही बार आकर अनेक अर्थ देता है।

questions.text: 'नयन' शब्द का सही संधि-विच्छेद कौन-सा है?
questions.explanation: नयन = ने + अन। जब 'ए' के बाद कोई भिन्न स्वर आता है तो 'ए' का 'अय्' हो जाता है (ए + अ = अय) — यह अयादि संधि है। 'नै + अन' से 'नायन' बनता, 'नयन' नहीं।

questions.text: 'माता-पिता' में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.explanation: माता-पिता का विग्रह है 'माता और पिता'। जिस समास में दोनों पद प्रधान हों और विग्रह करने पर 'और', 'या' जैसे योजक शब्द आएँ, वह द्वंद्व समास होता है।

questions.text: उत्प्रेक्षा अलंकार की पहचान प्रायः किन वाचक शब्दों से होती है?
questions.explanation: उत्प्रेक्षा में उपमेय में उपमान की संभावना या कल्पना की जाती है, जिसे 'मनु, मानो, जनु, जानो, मनहुँ' जैसे शब्द व्यक्त करते हैं। 'सा, सी, सम, सरिस' उपमा अलंकार के वाचक शब्द हैं।

questions.text: Choose the word most similar in meaning to BENEVOLENT.
questions.explanation: Benevolent comes from Latin 'bene' (well) and 'volent' (wishing), so it describes someone well-meaning and kind. Hostile, greedy and indifferent are close to its opposite.

questions.text: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to OBSTINATE.
questions.explanation: An obstinate person refuses to change their mind. Its opposite is flexible — willing to adapt. Stubborn and rigid are synonyms, and determined is close in meaning.

questions.text: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: 'Each of the boys / have finished / the assignment / before lunch.'
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular, so it takes a singular verb even when followed by 'of + plural noun'. The correct form is 'Each of the boys has finished the assignment before lunch.'

questions.text: Choose the best replacement for the words in brackets: 'He is senior (than me) by two years.'
questions.explanation: Comparatives borrowed from Latin — senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior — are followed by 'to', not 'than'. So the sentence should read 'He is senior to me by two years.'

questions.text: What does the idiom 'to burn the midnight oil' mean?
options: To study or work late into the night
To celebrate a festival with lamps
questions.explanation: The idiom comes from the days when people worked by oil lamps after dark. 'Burning the midnight oil' means staying up late to study or work.

questions.text: What does the phrase 'a blessing in disguise' mean?
options: A hidden enemy pretending to be a friend
Something that seems unfortunate at first but turns out to be good
A gift that is given secretly
questions.explanation: A blessing in disguise is an apparent misfortune that later proves beneficial — for example, missing a bus and so avoiding an accident.

questions.text: Arrange the sentences in a logical order. P: He decided to save a part of his salary every month. Q: Ravi wanted to buy a bicycle. R: After a year, he had saved enough money. S: So he bought the bicycle he had always dreamed of.
questions.explanation: The paragraph begins with Ravi's wish (Q), then his plan to save (P), the result after a year (R), and finally the purchase introduced by 'So' (S). The order QPRS follows cause and effect.

questions.text: Read: 'Bamboo is a grass, not a tree. Some species can grow up to about 90 cm in a single day, which makes bamboo one of the fastest-growing plants on Earth.' Which statement is supported by the passage?
options: Bamboo is the tallest tree on Earth
Every bamboo species grows 90 cm a day
Bamboo grows only in dry deserts
Bamboo is a grass, and some kinds grow very quickly
questions.explanation: The passage states that bamboo is a grass and that 'some species' can grow about 90 cm a day. It does not call bamboo a tree, claim all species grow that fast, or mention deserts.

questions.text: Which of these sentences is grammatically correct?
options: Neither the teacher nor the students were present.
Neither the teacher nor the students was present.
Neither the teacher or the students were present.
Neither of the teacher nor students were present.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' pairs with 'nor', and the verb agrees with the subject closer to it. Here the nearer subject is 'the students' (plural), so 'were' is correct.

questions.text: Choose the word that best fills the blank: 'The scientist's explanation was so ____ that even the children understood it.'
questions.explanation: Lucid means clear and easy to understand, which fits the result that even children understood. Obscure and cryptic mean hard to understand, and verbose means using too many words.

questions.text: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system; its diameter is about 11 times that of Earth. It is a gas giant made mostly of hydrogen and helium.

questions.text: On which date did the Constitution of India come into effect?
questions.explanation: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949, and it came into force on 26 January 1950, which is celebrated as Republic Day.

questions.text: Which Indian state has the longest coastline?
questions.explanation: Gujarat has India's longest coastline, roughly 1,600 km along the Arabian Sea, including the Gulf of Kutch and the Gulf of Khambhat.

questions.text: If 15% of a number is 45, what is the number?
questions.explanation: Let the number be x. Then 0.15x = 45, so x = 45 ÷ 0.15 = 300.

questions.text: A shopkeeper buys an article for ₹800 and sells it for ₹920. What is his profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Profit = 920 − 800 = ₹120. Profit % = (120 ÷ 800) × 100 = 15%. Profit percentage is always calculated on the cost price.

questions.text: Find the next number in the series: 3, 8, 15, 24, 35, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 5, 7, 9, 11, so the next difference is 13 and 35 + 13 = 48. Equivalently, each term is n² − 1 for n = 2, 3, 4, …, giving 7² − 1 = 48.

questions.text: The average of five numbers is 24. When one number is removed, the average of the remaining four becomes 22. What number was removed?
questions.explanation: The sum of five numbers = 5 × 24 = 120. The sum of the remaining four = 4 × 22 = 88. The removed number = 120 − 88 = 32.

questions.text: In a certain code, CAT is written as DBU. How is DOG written in that code?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by the next letter of the alphabet (C→D, A→B, T→U). Applying the same rule, D→E, O→P and G→H, so DOG becomes EPH.

questions.text: Pointing to a man, Riya said, 'He is the son of my grandfather's only son.' How is the man related to Riya?
questions.explanation: Riya's grandfather's only son must be Riya's father. The son of Riya's father is Riya's brother.

questions.text: Statements: All roses are flowers. Some flowers are red. Conclusions: I. Some roses are red. II. All flowers are roses. Which conclusion follows?
questions.explanation: The red flowers need not include any roses, so conclusion I does not follow. 'All roses are flowers' does not mean all flowers are roses, so conclusion II does not follow either.

questions.text: What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at exactly 3:00?
questions.explanation: Each hour mark on a clock is 360° ÷ 12 = 30° apart. At 3:00 the hands are three hour marks apart, so the angle is 3 × 30° = 90°.

questions.text: Aman walks 5 km north, turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right again and walks 5 km. How far is he now from his starting point?
questions.explanation: Going north 5 km, then east 3 km, then south 5 km cancels the northward distance. Aman ends 3 km due east of where he started.

questions.text: A train 150 m long passes a pole in 10 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.explanation: To pass a pole, the train covers its own length: speed = 150 m ÷ 10 s = 15 m/s. Converting, 15 × 18/5 = 54 km/h.

questions.text: What is the SI unit of electric current?
questions.explanation: The ampere is the SI base unit of electric current. The volt measures potential difference, the ohm measures resistance, and the coulomb measures electric charge.

questions.text: A pencil partly dipped in a glass of water appears bent at the water surface. This is due to:
questions.explanation: Light bends when it passes from water into air because its speed changes between the two media. This bending, called refraction, makes the submerged part of the pencil appear displaced.

questions.text: A ball is thrown vertically upward. Which statement is true at the highest point of its path?
options: Both velocity and acceleration are zero
Velocity is maximum and acceleration is zero
Acceleration is zero but velocity is not
Velocity is zero but acceleration is g, directed downward
questions.explanation: At the top the ball momentarily stops, so its velocity is zero. Gravity still acts on it, so its acceleration remains g (about 9.8 m/s²) downward throughout the flight.

questions.text: Which gas is commonly called 'laughing gas'?
questions.explanation: Nitrous oxide (N₂O) produces a mild euphoria when inhaled, which earned it the name laughing gas. It has long been used as an anaesthetic in dentistry and surgery.

questions.text: What is the pH of pure water at 25 °C?
questions.explanation: Pure water has equal concentrations of H⁺ and OH⁻ ions (10⁻⁷ mol/L each) at 25 °C, so it is neutral with pH 7. Values below 7 are acidic and above 7 are basic.

questions.text: Which of these metals is a liquid at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Mercury melts at about −39 °C, so it is liquid at room temperature; that is why it was used in thermometers. Sodium, aluminium and lead are solids.

questions.text: Which vitamin is produced in the human skin on exposure to sunlight?
questions.explanation: Ultraviolet-B rays from sunlight convert a cholesterol derivative in the skin into vitamin D. Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium for healthy bones.

questions.text: Which blood group is known as the universal donor?
questions.explanation: O-negative red blood cells carry no A, B or Rh antigens, so they can be given to patients of any blood group in an emergency. AB positive is the universal recipient.

questions.text: In which year did Mahatma Gandhi begin the Dandi March (Salt Satyagraha)?
questions.explanation: Gandhi set out from Sabarmati Ashram on 12 March 1930 and broke the salt law at Dandi on 6 April 1930, launching the Civil Disobedience Movement.

questions.text: Who presided over the first session of the Indian National Congress in 1885?
questions.explanation: The first session was held in Bombay in December 1885 under the presidency of Womesh Chunder Bonnerjee. A. O. Hume helped found the Congress but was not its first president.

questions.text: In August 1942, the All India Congress Committee passed the Quit India Resolution at its session held in which city?
questions.explanation: The Quit India Resolution was passed at the AICC session in Bombay on 8 August 1942, where Gandhi gave the call 'Do or Die' at Gowalia Tank Maidan.

questions.text: Which is the longest river that flows entirely within India?
questions.explanation: The Ganga is India's longest river overall but flows on into Bangladesh. The Godavari, about 1,465 km long, is the longest river flowing wholly within India and is called the Dakshin Ganga.

questions.text: Where is the headquarters of the United Nations located?
questions.explanation: The UN headquarters is in New York City. Geneva hosts the UN's European office, Paris hosts UNESCO, and The Hague is home to the International Court of Justice.
