questions.text: An article is sold for ₹2,000 (excluding tax) within the same state, and the GST rate on it is 18%. What is the amount of CGST charged?
questions.explanation: For an intra-state sale, GST is split equally into CGST and SGST, so each is 9% here. CGST = 9% of ₹2,000 = ₹180, and SGST is also ₹180.

questions.text: Rahul deposits ₹500 every month in a recurring deposit account for 2 years at 6% per annum simple interest. How much interest does he earn at maturity?
For what value of k does the quadratic equation x² − 6x + k = 0 have two equal real roots?
questions.explanation: Equal roots need the discriminant to be zero: b² − 4ac = 36 − 4k = 0, so k = 9.

questions.text: If A = [[2, 1], [3, 4]] (written row by row), what is A²?
questions.explanation: A² = A × A. First row: (2·2 + 1·3, 2·1 + 1·4) = (7, 6); second row: (3·2 + 4·3, 3·1 + 4·4) = (18, 19). Squaring each element separately is not matrix multiplication.

questions.text: Find the coordinates of the point that divides the line segment joining A(2, −3) and B(8, 6) internally in the ratio 1 : 2.
A solid metal sphere of radius 6 cm is melted and recast into a solid cone of base radius 6 cm. What is the height of the cone?
questions.explanation: Volume stays the same: (4/3)π(6)³ = (1/3)π(6)²h, so 288π = 12πh and h = 24 cm.

questions.text: A force of 10 N is applied perpendicular to a spanner at a distance of 0.25 m from the axis of rotation. What is the moment of the force?
questions.explanation: Moment of force = force × perpendicular distance from the axis of rotation = 10 N × 0.25 m = 2.5 N m.

questions.text: A machine has a mechanical advantage of 4 and a velocity ratio of 5. What is its efficiency?
questions.explanation: Efficiency = (mechanical advantage ÷ velocity ratio) × 100% = (4 ÷ 5) × 100% = 80%. A real machine always has an efficiency below 100% because of friction.

questions.chapter: Refraction of Light at Plane Surfaces
questions.topic: Refractive index and speed of light
questions.text: The refractive index of glass with respect to air is 1.5. If light travels at 3 × 10⁸ m/s in air, what is its speed in glass?
questions.explanation: Refractive index = speed of light in air ÷ speed of light in glass, so the speed in glass = (3 × 10⁸) ÷ 1.5 = 2 × 10⁸ m/s.

questions.text: Three resistors of 6 Ω each are connected in parallel. What is their equivalent resistance?
questions.explanation: In parallel, 1/R = 1/6 + 1/6 + 1/6 = 1/2, so R = 2 Ω. The equivalent resistance of a parallel combination is always less than the smallest individual resistance.

questions.text: How much heat is needed to change 50 g of ice at 0 °C into water at 20 °C? (Specific latent heat of fusion of ice = 336 J g⁻¹; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g⁻¹ °C⁻¹)
questions.explanation: Heat to melt the ice = mL = 50 × 336 = 16,800 J. Heat to warm the water from 0 °C to 20 °C = mcΔT = 50 × 4.2 × 20 = 4,200 J. Total = 21,000 J.

questions.text: What happens to the atomic number and mass number of a nucleus when it emits an alpha particle?
options: Atomic number decreases by 2 and mass number decreases by 4
Atomic number increases by 1 and mass number stays the same
Atomic number decreases by 4 and mass number decreases by 2
Atomic number and mass number both stay the same
questions.explanation: An alpha particle is a helium nucleus (2 protons and 2 neutrons), so the nucleus loses 2 from its atomic number and 4 from its mass number. Beta emission raises the atomic number by 1, and gamma emission changes neither.

questions.chapter: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties
questions.text: How does the atomic size of elements generally change across a period from left to right in the periodic table?
questions.explanation: Across a period, electrons are added to the same shell while the nuclear charge increases, so the outer electrons are pulled closer to the nucleus and the atomic size decreases.

questions.text: What volume does 8 g of oxygen gas (O₂) occupy at STP? (O = 16)
questions.explanation: The molar mass of O₂ is 32 g, so 8 g is 8 ÷ 32 = 0.25 mol. One mole of any gas occupies 22.4 L at STP, so the volume is 0.25 × 22.4 = 5.6 L.

questions.text: Which gases are liberated during the electrolysis of acidified water using platinum electrodes?
options: Hydrogen at the cathode and oxygen at the anode
Oxygen at the cathode and hydrogen at the anode
Hydrogen at the cathode and chlorine at the anode
questions.explanation: H⁺ ions gain electrons at the cathode to form hydrogen gas, while OH⁻ ions lose electrons at the anode to form oxygen gas. The two gases are collected in the volume ratio 2 : 1.

questions.topic: Action of NaOH on salt solutions
questions.text: What is the colour of the precipitate formed when sodium hydroxide solution is added to iron(II) sulphate solution?
questions.explanation: Fe²⁺ ions react with OH⁻ ions to form iron(II) hydroxide, Fe(OH)₂, a dirty green precipitate. Iron(III) salts give a reddish-brown precipitate of Fe(OH)₃ instead.

questions.text: Which drying agent is used to dry ammonia gas in the laboratory?
questions.explanation: Ammonia is basic, so it is dried with quicklime, a basic drying agent. Concentrated sulphuric acid and phosphorus pentoxide react with ammonia, and anhydrous calcium chloride forms an addition compound with it.

questions.text: How many structural (chain) isomers are possible for pentane, C₅H₁₂?
questions.explanation: Pentane has three chain isomers: n-pentane, 2-methylbutane (isopentane) and 2,2-dimethylpropane (neopentane).

questions.text: In which phase of mitosis do the chromosomes line up at the equatorial plane of the cell?
questions.explanation: During metaphase, spindle fibres attach to the centromeres and the chromosomes align at the equator, forming the metaphase plate. In anaphase the chromatids then separate and move to opposite poles.

questions.text: A homozygous tall pea plant (TT) is crossed with a homozygous dwarf plant (tt). What is the phenotypic ratio in the F₂ generation?
questions.explanation: All F₁ plants are Tt and tall. Selfing them gives TT, Tt and tt in the ratio 1 : 2 : 1, and because tallness is dominant the phenotypic ratio is 3 tall : 1 dwarf.

questions.text: Which apparatus measures the rate of water uptake by a leafy shoot, which closely reflects its rate of transpiration?
questions.explanation: A potometer (such as Ganong's potometer) measures how fast a cut shoot absorbs water, which is roughly equal to the water it loses by transpiration. A clinostat is used in tropism experiments, a respirometer for respiration and an auxanometer for growth.

questions.text: During photosynthesis, the oxygen released into the air comes from which substance?
questions.explanation: In the light-dependent phase, water molecules are split using light energy (photolysis of water), which releases oxygen. Carbon dioxide is used later to build glucose.

questions.text: Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart?
questions.explanation: The pulmonary veins bring oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium. They are the only veins that carry oxygenated blood, while the pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs.

questions.text: Deficiency of which hormone causes diabetes insipidus, in which a person passes large amounts of dilute urine?
questions.explanation: ADH (vasopressin), released from the posterior pituitary, makes the kidney tubules reabsorb water. Without enough ADH, water is not reabsorbed and large amounts of dilute urine are passed; a lack of insulin causes diabetes mellitus instead.

questions.text: Choose the correct verb to fill in the blank: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ present at the meeting yesterday.
questions.explanation: With 'neither … nor', the verb agrees with the subject closer to it. 'Students' is plural and the action happened in the past, so 'were' is correct.

questions.text: Which subscription (closing) is correct for a formal letter that begins with the salutation 'Dear Sir'?
questions.explanation: A formal letter addressed to someone not known by name, such as 'Dear Sir' or 'Dear Madam', ends with 'Yours faithfully'. Closings like 'Yours affectionately' belong only in informal letters.

questions.text: Choose the correct passive voice form of: 'The manager will sign the letters.'
options: The letters would be signed by the manager.
The letters are signed by the manager.
The letters will be signed by the manager.
The letters will have been signed by the manager.
questions.explanation: The simple future passive uses 'will be + past participle'. The object 'the letters' becomes the subject, giving 'The letters will be signed by the manager.'

questions.text: In 'The Merchant of Venice', who disguises herself as the young lawyer Balthazar to defend Antonio in court?
questions.explanation: Portia disguises herself as Balthazar, a young doctor of law recommended by her cousin Bellario, while Nerissa disguises herself as the lawyer's clerk. Portia's arguments save Antonio in the trial scene.

questions.text: In the trial scene of 'The Merchant of Venice', how does Portia defeat Shylock's claim on Antonio?
options: She proves that the bond was signed after the due date.
The bond allows a pound of flesh but not a single drop of blood.
She shows that Antonio has already repaid the loan in full.
She persuades the Duke to cancel all debts in Venice.
questions.explanation: Portia agrees that Shylock may take his pound of flesh but points out that the bond gives him 'no jot of blood'. Since he cannot cut the flesh without shedding blood, he would lose his lands and goods under Venetian law, so his claim collapses.

questions.text: जिस रस का स्थायी भाव 'शोक' होता है, वह कौन-सा रस है?
questions.explanation: करुण रस का स्थायी भाव शोक है; किसी प्रिय के बिछड़ने या नष्ट होने पर इसकी अनुभूति होती है। वीर रस का स्थायी भाव उत्साह, हास्य रस का हास और रौद्र रस का क्रोध होता है।

questions.text: 'राम द्वारा पुस्तक पढ़ी गई।' — इस वाक्य में कौन-सा वाच्य है?
questions.explanation: इस वाक्य में क्रिया 'पढ़ी गई' कर्म 'पुस्तक' के लिंग और वचन के अनुसार है तथा कर्ता के साथ 'द्वारा' लगा है, इसलिए यह कर्मवाच्य है।

questions.text: 'आँखों का तारा होना' मुहावरे का सही अर्थ क्या है?
questions.explanation: 'आँखों का तारा होना' का अर्थ है अत्यंत प्रिय होना, जैसे — इकलौता बेटा माँ की आँखों का तारा है।

questions.chapter: रचना के आधार पर वाक्य भेद
questions.text: 'जब वर्षा हुई, तब किसान प्रसन्न हो गए।' — रचना के आधार पर यह कौन-सा वाक्य है?
questions.explanation: इसमें 'तब किसान प्रसन्न हो गए' प्रधान उपवाक्य है और 'जब वर्षा हुई' उस पर आश्रित उपवाक्य है। प्रधान और आश्रित उपवाक्य से बने वाक्य को मिश्र वाक्य कहते हैं।

questions.text: पाठ्यक्रम में निर्धारित उपन्यास 'नया रास्ता' की लेखिका कौन हैं?
questions.explanation: 'नया रास्ता' उपन्यास की लेखिका सुषमा अग्रवाल हैं। यह उपन्यास दहेज और रंग-रूप के आधार पर होने वाले भेदभाव की समस्या पर आधारित है और इसकी नायिका मीनू है।

questions.text: According to the Constitution, what is the maximum gap allowed between two sessions of the Indian Parliament?
questions.explanation: Article 85 requires that no more than six months pass between the last sitting of one session and the first sitting of the next. So Parliament must meet at least twice a year.

questions.text: Which writ is issued by a court to order that a detained person be produced before it, so that the legality of the detention can be examined?
questions.explanation: Habeas Corpus means 'you may have the body' and protects personal liberty against unlawful detention. Mandamus orders an official to perform a duty, and Quo Warranto questions a person's right to hold a public office.

questions.text: At which place did the sepoys rise in open revolt on 10 May 1857, marking the start of the First War of Independence?
questions.explanation: On 10 May 1857, the sepoys at Meerut revolted, freed their imprisoned comrades and marched to Delhi. Mangal Pandey's earlier attack on British officers took place at Barrackpore in March 1857.

questions.chapter: Second Phase of the Indian National Movement
questions.text: In which year was the Partition of Bengal carried out by Lord Curzon?
questions.explanation: Bengal was partitioned in 1905 under Lord Curzon, which sparked the Swadeshi and Boycott Movement. The partition was annulled in 1911.

questions.text: Which event in December 1941 brought the United States directly into the Second World War?
questions.explanation: Japan's surprise attack on the US naval base at Pearl Harbor on 7 December 1941 led the USA to declare war. Germany's invasion of Poland in 1939 had started the war in Europe, and the Lusitania was sunk during the First World War.

questions.text: Where was the first summit of the Non-Aligned Movement held in 1961?
questions.explanation: The first NAM summit was held in Belgrade, Yugoslavia, in September 1961, with Nehru, Tito, Nasser, Sukarno and Nkrumah as its key leaders. The 1955 Bandung Conference of Asian and African nations had prepared the ground for it.

questions.text: On a topographical map with a scale of 1 : 50,000, what actual ground distance does 4 cm on the map represent?
questions.explanation: 1 cm on the map = 50,000 cm = 0.5 km on the ground, so 4 cm = 4 × 0.5 km = 2 km.

questions.text: Which winds bring most of the rainfall to the Tamil Nadu coast during October to December?
questions.explanation: The north-east (retreating) monsoon winds pick up moisture over the Bay of Bengal and bring winter rain to the Coromandel coast of Tamil Nadu. Western disturbances bring winter rain to north-west India, and the Loo is a hot, dry summer wind.

questions.text: Black soil (regur) is best suited for growing which crop?
questions.explanation: Black soil is rich in clay, retains moisture well and contains lime, iron and magnesia, which makes it ideal for cotton; it is also called black cotton soil.

questions.text: Which variety of iron ore has the highest iron content?
questions.explanation: Magnetite is the finest iron ore, with an iron content of about 70% or more. Hematite has a slightly lower iron content, while limonite and siderite are poorer ores.

questions.text: Which of the following is a kharif crop?
questions.explanation: Kharif crops are sown with the onset of the south-west monsoon in June–July and harvested in autumn; rice is the main kharif crop. Wheat, mustard and gram are rabi crops sown in winter.

questions.text: The North–South Corridor of India's National Highways Development Project connects which two places?
questions.explanation: The North–South Corridor links Srinagar in the north with Kanyakumari in the south. The East–West Corridor connects Silchar in Assam with Porbandar in Gujarat.

questions.text: Which object-oriented principle allows a class to acquire the data members and methods of another class?
questions.explanation: Inheritance lets a subclass reuse the properties and behaviour of a superclass (using the keyword extends in Java), which promotes code reusability.

questions.text: A method is defined as: static int square(int n) { return n * n; } What is printed by System.out.println(square(3) + square(4)); ?
questions.explanation: square(3) returns 9 and square(4) returns 16. Both are int values, so + performs numeric addition and 25 is printed; the values would be joined as text only if a String were involved.

questions.text: Which statement about a constructor in Java is correct?
options: It must always return an int value.
It is executed only when a method named init() is called.
It must have a name different from the class name.
It has the same name as the class and no return type.
questions.explanation: A constructor has the same name as its class and no return type, not even void. It is invoked automatically when an object is created with the new keyword.

questions.text: What is the value of the expression Integer.parseInt("45") + 5 in Java?
questions.explanation: Integer.parseInt("45") converts the String "45" into the int value 45, so the expression is integer addition: 45 + 5 = 50.

questions.text: What is printed by this code? int[] a = {4, 7, 1, 9}; int s = 0; for (int i = 1; i < a.length; i += 2) s += a[i]; System.out.println(s);
questions.explanation: The loop visits only indices 1 and 3 (i = 1, then 3; at i = 5 the loop stops). So s = a[1] + a[3] = 7 + 9 = 16.

questions.text: What does "COMPUTER".substring(2, 5) return in Java?
questions.explanation: Indexing starts at 0, and substring(begin, end) returns the characters from index begin up to end − 1. Indices 2, 3 and 4 hold M, P and U, so the result is "MPU".

questions.text: Who among the following is an internal user of accounting information?
questions.explanation: Internal users are people inside the organisation, such as owners and managers, who use accounting information for planning, control and decision-making. Creditors, tax authorities and investors are external users.

questions.text: Under the money measurement concept, which of the following events will be recorded in the books of accounts?
options: Appointment of a new sales manager
A competitor opening a shop nearby
questions.explanation: The money measurement concept says only transactions and events that can be expressed in money terms are recorded. A credit sale of ₹20,000 has a money value; the other events, however important, cannot be measured reliably in money.

questions.text: A firm has total assets of ₹2,40,000 and the owner's capital is ₹1,65,000. What are its outside liabilities?
questions.explanation: From the accounting equation Assets = Liabilities + Capital, Liabilities = Assets − Capital = ₹2,40,000 − ₹1,65,000 = ₹75,000.

questions.text: A machine is bought for ₹1,00,000. Its estimated scrap value is ₹10,000 and its useful life is 5 years. What is the annual depreciation under the straight line method?
questions.explanation: Under the straight line method, annual depreciation = (Cost − Scrap value) ÷ Useful life = (₹1,00,000 − ₹10,000) ÷ 5 = ₹18,000, charged equally every year.

questions.chapter: Trial Balance and Rectification of Errors
questions.topic: Errors not disclosed by trial balance
questions.text: Which of the following errors will NOT affect the agreement of the trial balance?
options: Posting an amount to the wrong side of an account
Purchase of machinery debited to the Purchases account
Posting only the debit side of a journal entry
questions.explanation: Debiting machinery to the Purchases account is an error of principle: the debit is still recorded for the correct amount, so both sides of the trial balance stay equal. Casting errors, wrong-side postings and one-sided postings make the trial balance disagree.

questions.text: If there is no partnership deed, in what ratio do partners share the profits of the firm?
options: In the ratio of their capitals
In the ratio of time devoted to the business
As decided by the senior-most partner
questions.explanation: Under the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, when there is no deed, profits and losses are shared equally, no interest is allowed on capitals and no salary is paid to partners.

questions.chapter: Reconstitution of a Partnership Firm – Admission of a Partner
questions.text: A and B share profits in the ratio 3 : 2. C is admitted for a 1/5 share, which he takes equally from A and B. What is the new profit-sharing ratio of A, B and C?
questions.explanation: C gets 1/5 = 2/10, taking 1/10 from each partner. A: 6/10 − 1/10 = 5/10; B: 4/10 − 1/10 = 3/10; C: 2/10. So the new ratio is 5 : 3 : 2.

questions.text: When a company issues shares at a premium, the amount of premium is credited to:
questions.explanation: Premium is the amount received above the face value of shares. It is credited to the Securities Premium Account, which can be used only for the purposes allowed under Section 52 of the Companies Act, 2013.

questions.text: Debentures of ₹1,00,000 are issued at a discount of 5% and are redeemable at a premium of 10%. What is the amount of 'Loss on Issue of Debentures'?
questions.explanation: Loss on issue includes the discount allowed (5% of ₹1,00,000 = ₹5,000) plus the premium payable on redemption (10% of ₹1,00,000 = ₹10,000), so it is ₹15,000.

questions.text: A company has current assets of ₹4,00,000, which include inventory of ₹1,00,000 and no prepaid expenses. Its current liabilities are ₹2,00,000. What is its quick ratio?
questions.explanation: Quick assets = Current assets − Inventory − Prepaid expenses = ₹4,00,000 − ₹1,00,000 = ₹3,00,000. Quick ratio = ₹3,00,000 ÷ ₹2,00,000 = 1.5 : 1.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of an 'auxiliary to trade'?
questions.explanation: Auxiliaries to trade are activities that help trade run smoothly, such as transport, banking, insurance, warehousing and advertising. Mining and fishing are extractive industries, and cement making is manufacturing.

questions.text: What is the nature of the liability of a sole proprietor?
options: Limited to the amount of guarantee
questions.explanation: A sole proprietor has unlimited liability: if business assets are not enough to pay its debts, the owner's personal assets can be used, because the law does not treat the business and its owner as separate.

questions.text: A company in which at least 51% of the paid-up share capital is held by the government is known as a:
questions.explanation: Under the Companies Act, a government company is one in which not less than 51% of the paid-up share capital is held by the Central Government, State Government(s), or both. It is registered under the Companies Act like any other company.

questions.text: The portion of net profit that a company keeps for reinvestment in the business instead of distributing it as dividend is known as:
questions.explanation: Retained earnings, also called ploughing back of profits, are an internal source of owners' funds. They involve no explicit cost or flotation charges, unlike borrowed funds.

questions.text: Which document is issued by a shipping company as an official receipt of goods placed on its vessel and as an undertaking to carry them to the port of destination?
questions.explanation: A bill of lading is both a receipt for goods loaded on the ship and the shipping company's undertaking to carry them to the destination; it also serves as a document of title. A mate's receipt is only an acknowledgement issued by the ship's officer when cargo is loaded.

questions.text: Management is described as 'all-pervasive' because it:
options: Is needed only in large business firms
Is required in all types of organisations and at all levels
Is concerned only with making profits
Is the same as administration in government offices
questions.explanation: Management activities are common to all organisations — business or non-business, small or large — and to every level within them. This universal presence is what makes management all-pervasive.

questions.text: According to Henri Fayol's principle of 'unity of command', an employee should:
options: Work under one plan along with others who have the same objective
Be treated equally with other employees
Receive orders from only one superior
Be given authority equal to his responsibility
questions.explanation: Unity of command means each employee should receive orders from, and be accountable to, only one boss, which avoids confusion and conflict. 'One head, one plan' for activities with the same objective is the separate principle of unity of direction.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a single-use plan?
questions.explanation: Single-use plans are made for a one-time event or a specific period and include budgets, programmes and projects. Policies, procedures, methods and rules are standing plans that are used repeatedly.

questions.text: Which is the first step in the staffing process?
questions.explanation: Staffing begins by estimating how many and what kind of employees are needed, through workload and workforce analysis. Only then does the firm recruit, select, place, train and appraise people.

questions.text: Which of the following factors favours using MORE debt in a company's capital structure?
options: Return on investment lower than the cost of debt
A very low rate of tax
questions.explanation: A high interest coverage ratio shows that earnings comfortably cover interest payments, so the company can safely take on more debt. Uncertain cash flows, an ROI below the cost of debt and a low tax rate (which reduces the tax benefit of interest) all argue for less debt.

questions.text: Data collected for the first time by an investigator for a specific purpose is called:
questions.explanation: Primary data are original data collected first-hand by the investigator, for example through surveys or interviews. Secondary data have already been collected by someone else and are reused.

questions.text: What is the median of the observations 4, 10, 6, 15, 8?
questions.explanation: Arrange the data in ascending order: 4, 6, 8, 10, 15. With 5 observations, the median is the middle (3rd) value, which is 8. The value 8.6 is the arithmetic mean, not the median.

questions.text: When the total utility from consuming a good reaches its maximum, marginal utility is:
questions.explanation: Marginal utility is the change in total utility from consuming one more unit. Total utility rises while MU is positive, is at its maximum when MU becomes zero, and falls when MU turns negative.

questions.text: What is the shape of the short-run average fixed cost (AFC) curve?
questions.explanation: Total fixed cost stays constant, so AFC = TFC ÷ Q falls continuously as output rises but never touches zero. Since AFC × Q always equals the same TFC, the AFC curve is a rectangular hyperbola.

questions.chapter: The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition
questions.text: Under perfect competition, the demand (average revenue) curve faced by an individual firm is:
questions.explanation: A perfectly competitive firm is a price taker: it can sell any quantity at the market price set by industry demand and supply. So its AR (= MR) curve is a horizontal line at that price, which means it is perfectly elastic.

questions.text: Gross Domestic Product at market price minus depreciation is equal to:
options: Gross National Product at market price
Net Domestic Product at market price
questions.explanation: Gross aggregates include depreciation (consumption of fixed capital), while 'net' aggregates exclude it. So GDP at market price − Depreciation = NDP at market price.

questions.text: The rate at which the Reserve Bank of India lends short-term funds to commercial banks against government securities is called the:
questions.explanation: Under a repurchase agreement, the RBI lends to commercial banks at the repo rate. Raising the repo rate makes borrowing costlier for banks and helps control inflation; the reverse repo rate is the rate at which the RBI borrows from banks.

questions.text: If the marginal propensity to consume (MPC) is 0.8, what is the value of the investment multiplier?
questions.explanation: Multiplier k = 1 ÷ (1 − MPC) = 1 ÷ (1 − 0.8) = 1 ÷ 0.2 = 5. So an increase in investment raises national income by five times that increase.

questions.text: Fiscal deficit in a government budget is equal to:
options: Total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings
questions.explanation: Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure − (Revenue receipts + non-debt capital receipts), which equals the government's total borrowing requirement. Revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts is the revenue deficit, and fiscal deficit minus interest payments is the primary deficit.

questions.chapter: Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation: An Appraisal
questions.text: In which year did India introduce the New Economic Policy of liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation?
questions.explanation: Facing a severe balance of payments crisis, India launched its economic reforms — the New Economic Policy — in 1991, opening the economy to greater private and foreign participation.

questions.text: The cuneiform script, one of the earliest forms of writing, developed in:
questions.explanation: The first known writing in Mesopotamia, from about 3200 BCE, was cuneiform — wedge-shaped signs pressed into wet clay tablets. It was used to keep records of trade and administration in early cities.

questions.text: The Roman Empire at its height spread across which three continents?
questions.explanation: The Roman Empire covered much of Europe, the Fertile Crescent in West Asia and North Africa, all linked around the Mediterranean Sea — hence 'an empire across three continents'.

questions.text: In which year was Temujin proclaimed 'Genghis Khan', the Oceanic Khan or Universal Ruler of the Mongols?
questions.explanation: At a quriltai (assembly of chiefs) in 1206, Temujin was proclaimed Genghis Khan. He went on to build a vast empire and died in 1227; Baghdad was sacked by his grandson Hulegu in 1258.

questions.text: In medieval western Europe, society was described as consisting of three orders. These were:
questions.explanation: French priests described society as made up of three orders: those who prayed (the clergy), those who fought (the nobility) and those who worked (the peasants).

questions.text: Who founded the Guomindang (Kuomintang) and is regarded as the founder of modern China?
questions.explanation: Sun Yat-sen led the 1911 revolution that ended the Manchu empire and founded the Guomindang; his Three Principles (nationalism, democracy and socialism) shaped modern China. Chiang Kai-shek later led the Guomindang, and Mao Zedong led the Communist Party.

questions.text: At which Harappan site was the 'Great Bath' discovered?
questions.explanation: The Great Bath, a large rectangular tank in the citadel of Mohenjodaro, was made watertight with bricks set in gypsum mortar. Scholars think it was used for special ritual bathing.

questions.text: The Prayaga Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar Inscription) praising Samudragupta was composed by:
questions.explanation: Harishena, the court poet of Samudragupta, composed the Prayaga Prashasti in Sanskrit. Prashastis like this praised rulers and are valuable sources for reconstructing Gupta history.

questions.text: The Great Stupa at Sanchi is located in which present-day state?
questions.explanation: Sanchi lies near Bhopal in Madhya Pradesh. Its stupa, with richly carved gateways, survived partly because the rulers of Bhopal, Shahjehan Begum and Sultan Jehan Begum, funded its preservation.

questions.text: Ibn Battuta, the traveller from Morocco, wrote an account of his travels in Arabic known as the:
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta's travel account, the Rihla, describes social and cultural life in the subcontinent in the fourteenth century, including the court of Muhammad bin Tughlaq. Kitab-ul-Hind was written by Al-Biruni.

questions.text: Who introduced the 'Objectives Resolution' in the Constituent Assembly on 13 December 1946?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution, which set out the ideals of the Constitution — an independent sovereign republic guaranteeing justice, equality and freedom. It later shaped the Preamble.

questions.text: When did the Constituent Assembly of India hold its first sitting?
questions.explanation: The Constituent Assembly first met on 9 December 1946. It adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949, and the Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950.

questions.text: Which Fundamental Right did Dr B.R. Ambedkar call the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32) lets citizens approach the courts directly when their fundamental rights are violated. Without it the other rights could not be enforced, which is why Ambedkar called it the heart and soul of the Constitution.

questions.text: Which electoral system is used in India for elections to the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: Under FPTP, the candidate with the most votes in a constituency wins, even without a majority. Proportional representation through the single transferable vote is used for Rajya Sabha and presidential elections.

questions.text: The President of India is elected by:
options: Members of the Lok Sabha only
An electoral college of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and of the State Legislative Assemblies
The Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers
questions.explanation: The President is elected indirectly by an electoral college of elected MPs and elected MLAs (including those of Delhi and Puducherry), using proportional representation by single transferable vote.

questions.text: J.S. Mill argued that a person's liberty can be restricted only to prevent harm to others. This idea is known as the:
questions.explanation: Mill's harm principle distinguishes self-regarding actions, which affect only the individual, from other-regarding actions that can harm others. Only the latter may be restricted by the state or society.

questions.text: In which year did the Soviet Union disintegrate?
questions.explanation: The USSR broke up in December 1991 into fifteen independent countries, ending the bipolar Cold War world. The Berlin Wall had fallen earlier, in 1989.

questions.text: How many permanent members does the UN Security Council have?
questions.explanation: The Security Council has five permanent members with veto power — the US, Russia, the UK, France and China — plus ten non-permanent members elected for two-year terms, making fifteen in all.

questions.text: The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) was established in:
questions.explanation: SAARC was set up in 1985 by South Asian states to promote cooperation through multilateral means. Its members later signed the South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) agreement in 2004.

questions.text: When was the first general election held in independent India?
questions.explanation: India's first general election was held between October 1951 and February 1952 with universal adult franchise. The Indian National Congress won a large majority, beginning an era of one-party dominance.

questions.text: The Emergency declared in June 1975 on the grounds of 'internal disturbance' was proclaimed under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 352 provides for a national emergency. In June 1975 it was invoked citing internal disturbance, and fundamental rights were curtailed until the emergency ended in 1977. Article 356 covers President's Rule in states and Article 360 a financial emergency.

questions.text: The boundary that separates the Earth's crust from the mantle is called the:
questions.explanation: The Mohorovicic discontinuity (Moho) marks the change from crust to mantle, where seismic wave velocities increase sharply. The Gutenberg discontinuity lies between the mantle and the core.

questions.text: In which layer of the atmosphere do almost all weather phenomena take place?
questions.explanation: The troposphere, the lowest layer, holds most of the atmosphere's water vapour and dust. Clouds, rain and storms all occur here, and temperature falls with height at about 1°C for every 165 m.

questions.text: Who proposed the theory of continental drift in 1912?
questions.explanation: Alfred Wegener suggested that all continents once formed a single supercontinent, Pangaea, which broke up and drifted apart. Harry Hess later proposed sea-floor spreading, and Arthur Holmes suggested convection currents in the mantle.

questions.text: The Tropic of Cancer passes through how many states of India?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer (23°30′N) crosses eight states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram, dividing India into almost equal halves.

questions.text: Which region of India receives a large part of its rainfall in winter from the north-east (retreating) monsoon?
questions.explanation: During October–December, the retreating north-east monsoon picks up moisture over the Bay of Bengal and brings rain to the Coromandel coast of Tamil Nadu, which stays comparatively dry during the south-west monsoon.

questions.text: The first stage of the demographic transition theory is characterised by:
options: Low birth rate and low death rate
High birth rate and high death rate
High birth rate and declining death rate
Low birth rate and high death rate
questions.explanation: In the first stage, high fertility is offset by high mortality from epidemics and food shortages, so population grows slowly. In later stages death rates fall first, followed by birth rates.

questions.text: Which of the following is a primary activity?
questions.explanation: Primary activities depend directly on the environment and natural resources, such as hunting, gathering, fishing, farming, forestry and mining. Manufacturing is a secondary activity, while banking and software development are tertiary/quaternary activities.

questions.text: The Trans-Siberian Railway connects:
questions.explanation: The Trans-Siberian Railway runs from St Petersburg in the west to Vladivostok on the Pacific coast. It is the longest double-tracked, electrified trans-continental railway in the world and links Asian Russia with European markets.

questions.text: Which of the following is a kharif crop in India?
questions.explanation: Kharif crops are sown with the onset of the south-west monsoon and harvested in autumn; rice, cotton, maize and jowar are examples. Wheat, mustard and gram are rabi crops grown in winter.

questions.chapter: Population: Distribution, Density, Growth and Composition
questions.text: According to Census 2011, which state of India had the highest population density?
questions.explanation: Census 2011 recorded Bihar's density at 1,106 persons per sq km, the highest among states, followed by West Bengal (1,028) and Kerala (860). India's average density was 382 persons per sq km.
